oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Factors Influencing the Development of the SSE in Rural Tunisia
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study examines the factors that influence the development of the social and solidarity economy (SSE) in rural northwest Tunisia. Through 136 semi-structured interviews analyzed using lexicometric discourse methods, the study identifies three major barriers to its development and highlights the emergence of hybrid SSE models that combine traditional solidarity networks with international, donor-supported initiatives. These models show promise in rebuilding trust and enhancing collective action. The policy recommendations emphasize the need for targeted education, stronger legal frameworks, and sustainable funding to encourage the adoption of the SSE in marginalized rural areas. These findings contribute to a broader understanding of how local culture, institutional path dependency, and external interventions interact to shape SSE trajectories in Tunisia and other African countries.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les organisations chrétiennes de développement aux États-Unis du temps de la guerre froide : des enjeux très politiques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article highlights the strategic and diplomatic issues surrounding faith-based development NGOs which have received little attention to date. The analysis focuses on the United States, a major player in the Cold War and international aid. In particular, it highlights the wide diversity of approaches to poverty in the Global South taken by different Christian and missionary traditions. The argument is based on open sources: activity reports, memoirs of development actors, extensive bibliographic resources, etc. Such a corpus allows for a more detailed analysis of the instrumentalisation of Christian charitable organisations funded by public authorities to serve US foreign policy.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Insécurisation gouvernée et enjeux fonciers de la transition verte
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Drawing on the case of the Noor Midelt solar complex, this article examines the land-related effects of the energy transition in Morocco. Based on a socio-anthropological field study conducted between 2019 and 2024, it shows how domanial authority, selective compensation, and the conditional tolerance of irregular practices contribute to a regime of “governed insecurity”. This mode of governance relies on the ambiguous plurality of land tenure statuses and the fragmentation of customary land use rights. It keeps rural populations in a state of uncertainty, limiting their ability to claim rights, excluding them from the project’s benefits, while intermittently integrating them into its operation. The Midelt case highlights the contradictions of an energy transition that, under the banner of sustainability, redefines spatial practices in an authoritarian manner and denies territorial attachments not recognized by the state.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Intermédiation coercitive dans l’économie mondiale
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the link between the plantation economy and armed violence. Drawing on the case of an agro-industrial area in the Colombian Caribbean, it explores the articulation of a local struggle over the exploitation and appropriation of two parcels of land and the national armed conflict between 1994 and 2000. On the basis of legal archives and interviews, it shows that armed violence develops in direct interaction with movements in the international market and with local disputes over land and labour. It examines the engagement of armed actors in coercive brokerage within the local regime of control over labour and natural resources.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La montagne-sportive au Maroc : entre confiscation, préservation et marchandisation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This contribution addresses certain dynamics of the development of natural spaces in Morocco based on surveys devoted to mountain sports in the country. The article begins with an ethnography of mountain sports and sports tourism in the Moroccan Atlas, following two lines of thought: mountain sports have become established in this country as an ‘inner’ elsewhere; at the same time, the destination ‘Moroccan mountains’ represents a centrality constructed ‘from the outside’ via the international sports tourism market. This tension inherent in mountain sports in Morocco raises questions about the relationship between environmentalism and commercialism at a time when consumer capitalism has a strong hold on sport, including ‘nature’ sports.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les nouveaux fronts collectifs de l’arganiculture au Maroc, heurs et malheurs du partenariat public-commun
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Sustainable development and climate change mitigation policies promoted by international organisations are mobilising large community land holdings based on the public-common partnership model. An analysis of the first collective argan farming pilot project in Morocco sheds light on the difficulties of regenerating argan forests in a context of demographic decline. Invoking the principle of land and agricultural commons makes it possible to move beyond an approach that focuses on collectives/communities as mere beneficiaries and providers of land for the benefit of a public-private project. The concept of the commons makes it possible to understand the different forms of attachment to the land and trees and to recognise specific knowledge and skills. Indeed, they make it possible to overcome the limitations and shortcomings of agricultural development projects based on the liberal principle of the public procurement contracts.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Tunisie : la néolibéralisation inachevée
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Drawing on the analysis of two conflicts related to the socio-environmental spillovers of the phosphate processing industry in the regions of Sfax and Gabes, this article examines the effects of the 2011 moment on the neoliberalisation of pollution governance in Tunisia. Under the Ben Ali regime, the adoption of an environmental regulatory framework inspired by neoliberal doctrine had already encountered limitations when faced with the state’s desire for control. After 2011, while neoliberal governance modalities were reinforced and the industrial space was reorganized to serve territorial competitiveness, it was an old solution – the granting of compensations to protesting groups – that ultimately helped to resolve the conflicts.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Terres pastorales : néolibéralisme de la nature et conflits locaux
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article offers a sociological analysis of the processes of neoliberalization of pastoral lands in the Tiznit region of Southern Morocco, based on a case study focused on agricultural and pastoral policies implemented since the 2000s. It shows how various actors engage in market-oriented logics regarding pastoral resources. This logic contributes to the reconfiguration of access regimes, the exclusion of traditional users and fuels two levels of conflict: inter- and intra-community. Based on qualitative fieldwork (2021–2023), the study reveals a state that, under the guise of sustainability, promotes the economic valorization of pastoral lands at the expense of customary arrangements.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les eaux non conventionnelles dans le bassin de l’oued El Kebir (Algérie-Tunisie) : une lecture depuis les Sustainability Transition Studies
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines investments in so-called ‘unconventional’ water infrastructure in a transboundary basin between Algeria and Tunisia. It is based on a comparative, multi-scale study of water policies in order to question the discourse promoting these techniques as an innovative way of responding to declining water availability linked to climate change. The article shows that these projects are not new and overlap with previous socio-technical regimes based on large-scale freshwater extraction. This socio-technical hybridisation, observed in particular in the El Kebir basin, reflects increased pressure on aquifers, which threatens the sustainability of hydrosystems.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le statut des terres collectives dans la dynamique de néolibéralisation de l’agriculture au Maroc : une illustration dans la vallée de Todgha
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Morocco is actively integrating into the international division of labour through agriculture, which is transforming access to land. In the Todgha Valley, under the influence of neoliberal policies, these dynamics are changing land use rights. The study is based on field research to understand the historical evolution of the status of collective land. Community use is evolving towards increasing individual appropriation, marked by three major historical phases. These lands are becoming commodities coveted by investors, redefining the rights of beneficiaries and exacerbating land conflicts, while still relying partially on customary law.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Enseigner le français langue étrangère à l’université avec et par la bande dessinée : l’exemple de Tout seul de Christophe Chabouté
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article presents a pedagogical approach centered on Christophe Chabouté’s graphic novel (bande dessinée) Tout seul (2008) , integrated into a French as a Foreign Language course at the Department of French and Francophone Studies at the University of Zadar (Croatia). The teaching methodology is based on the four modalities outlined by Kirtley et al. (2020), which involve teaching about comics, with comics, through comics, and through producing comics as means of processing thinking and learning.The results indicate that Tout seul is a valuable pedagogical tool for a university-level audience: its use in the teaching of French as a foreign language helps develop linguistic and transversal skills, enhances motivation for learning and reading in French, and encourages the adoption of autonomous learning strategies. Moreover, the implemented approach strengthens multimodal reading skills and allows students to deepen their understanding of a key medium of Francophone culture—bande dessinée—and its expressive possibilities. These findings support a more systematic integration of this type of teaching method into university-level French as a Foreign Language programs.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Entre les lignes et les images : redessiner l’apprentissage par le biais d’un graphic memoir
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This contribution explores the educational potential of Nora Krug’s Heimat (2018), a graphic memoir that combines graphic storytelling, visual design, and multilingual dimensions. Heimat offers innovative pedagogical perspectives for teaching foreign languages and adopting transdisciplinary approaches. The analysis demonstrates how this work, which blurs the boundaries between autobiography, documentation, and fiction, fosters cross-disciplinary engagement—encompassing literary, linguistic, historical, artistic, and cultural perspectives.The article first examines the multimodal aspects of Heimat and their ability to challenge traditional literary hierarchies. Through its hybrid formats and non-linear structure, the work invites a redefinition of literature within educational contexts. It also serves as a valuable resource for addressing issues of transgenerational memory, cultural identity, and collective guilt associated with the Nazi regime.Three pedagogical perspectives are proposed for post-compulsory education (15–19 years): Using Heimat when teaching German as a foreign language, a multilingual approach that incorporates various linguistic versions of the graphic memoir, and an interdisciplinary perspective integrating language, history, and visual arts. These proposals include collaborative activities, translation analyses, and artistic projects, providing new ways to engage with educational practices and incorporate graphic memoirs. Based on these reflections, this article advocates for rethinking the potential and (non-)legitimacy of graphic memoirs and comics in educational contexts.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Exploiter la grammaire du portugais à travers la bande dessinée
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines how formal aspects at the level of grammar, phonetics and vocabulary of Brazilian Portuguese (BP) can be exploited from the reading of a comic, in a private lesson in France for a learner with a Lusophone family. The corpus consists of the recording of the session, centered on the reading of a comic from the Chico Bento series, created by Maurício de Sousa, presenting the diatopic variation “caipira” and the original Tupi language. The qualitative analysis (Denzin and Lincoln 2006) considers the pedagogical exploitation of the phonetic representation of five examples of “caipira” and six examples of Tupi vocabulary. The results show that the comic was used to work on reading, oral production and grammatical systematization of BP during the session. The proposed activity enabled the situated use of Portuguese during the discussion between the learner and the teacher, interspersed with moments of focus on the linguistic form. The teacher was able to reflect on the notion of error as a deviation from the grammatical norm (Bagno 2012) and linguistic variation with the learner. This seems to contribute to the student’s transmission of Portuguese, since he has started reading the comics he worked on in the classroom to his children, adapting the dialogues to standard Portuguese.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les affordances médiatiques de la bande dessinée pour l’enseignement de la langue parlée en FLE
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article argues that didactic reflection on the use of comics in teaching French as a foreign language should be based on a better understanding of the specificity of this medium, which cannot be reduced to just another literary genre or a simple visual aid. This article starts from the notion of media affordance to examine how comics represent the target language, particularly in speech bubbles. These are then considered from the perspective of mediation for the acquisition of spoken French.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Que devient la bande dessinée dans les supports médiatiques pédagogiques ? Le cas de la représentation de l’oral spontané dans deux manuels de FLE
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the use of “authentic comics” (Giroud 2021) as a pedagogical resource in the teaching of French as a Foreign Language (FLE), with a particular focus on the representation of spoken language. Through a comparative analysis of two textbooks based on the communicative approach—La BD, la bande dessinée satirique dans la classe de français langue étrangère (1987) and Oxford French Cartoon-strip Vocabulary Builder (2000)—the study highlights the gap between the pedagogical intentions declared by the authors and their actual implementation, particularly regarding the teaching of spoken French. The article explores how authentic comics are adapted when transposed into pedagogical materials, for didactic and/or commercial reasons, and how these adaptations may compromise certain teaching objectives, thereby underscoring the complex editorial and pedagogical challenges involved in integrating comics into language textbooks.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Stylisation de l’oralité en bande dessinée : variation, représentations du vernaculaire urbain contemporain et perspectives didactiques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the representation of orality and linguistic variation in a corpus of so-called “banlieue” comics published between 2008 and 2023. Drawing on a comparison with the Multicultural Paris French corpus (Gadet et al. 2017) and two film corpora, it highlights the stylization of certain features emblematic of Contemporary Urban Vernacular French (appellatives, interrogative and exclamative forms), whose use remains deliberately limited in order to avoid caricature. The analysis also underlines the specificity of the graphic medium, which relies on phonography (Mahrer 2017) and various visual devices to produce an effect of orality. These linguistic and graphic choices contribute to the representation of social practices and character identities. Finally, the article proposes didactic applications for the teaching of French as a foreign language at advanced levels, showing how comics can serve as a critical resource fostering sociolinguistic awareness and reflection on representations of contemporary French.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Wesh ou ouèche ? Les trucages orthographiques comme contrat de lecture dans la série d’albums Les Cahiers d’Esther de Riad Sattouf
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article combines a sociolinguistic and literary approach to examine representations of spoken French in a corpus of graphic literature. It analyzes the orthographic variations of wesh/ouèche in Les Cahiers d’Esther by Riad Sattouf, exploring their sociolinguistic and narrative functions to evaluate their potential use as a pedagogical tool in language classrooms. The orthographic choices, far from being mere reproductions of “youth speech”, contribute to character construction and reflect the social judgments of the narrator, Esther. These choices are part of a reading contract that draws on shared reader expectations about language and its variations. The form wesh is associated with speakers from lower social groups, while ouèche signifies an appropriation (crossing) by privileged speakers. These forms thus illustrate power dynamics and social stratifications. Narratively, these spellings enhance character development, particularly that of Esther, for whom the use of ouèche becomes both a typifying and distinctive feature. The representation of orality reveals a tension between fidelity to linguistic usage and literary stylization.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: De la Galice à Angoulême : parcours multilingues d’édition de bandes dessinées et usages didactiques de ces produits culturels en cours de langue
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study focuses on the multilingual publishing market through the journey of two comics first published on the Franco-Belgian market by Spanish authors, Celle qui parle by Alicia Jaraba Abellán and Des maux à dire by Bea Lema. Their multilingual experiences echo the themes of communication and power issues addressed in the teaching of multilingualism/languages. How do these works circulate between languages by adapting to French- and Spanish-speaking comic book readers? How is multilingual writing constructed for the authors and the text-image link? Through a comparative study of different linguistic versions and interviews with the authors, we show the place of multilingualisms in their writing and publishing journeys. Beyond the linguistic aspect, their multisensory understanding as comic book authors stages multisemiotic representations. This work beyond language appears promising for addressing complex societal themes at all levels of the language course.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Voyager en bande dessinée dans « l’Empire des signes »
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Japan has become a favorite destination for comics authors, who are drawn to Japanese culture and its products, particularly in the field of graphic arts. Since the advent of travel writing in comics or graphic travelogues, Japan has emerged as a popular subject, depicted in a multitude of ways, frequently oscillating between the documentary and encyclopaedic, and the more personal and intimate. Based on a comprehensive collection of French-language comics, as well as other languages comics, we present an analysis of these narratives, which give rise to a series of recurring themes. These albums describe encounters with forms of alterity, which are sometimes presented in stereotyped ways, particularly in terms of gender relations. The authors' ethnography of everyday life seldom prompts reflection on their own Western perspective, and instead offers a form of orientalism that is also visually represented in the relationship with language. Japanese is frequently inadequately mastered and simplified, and the language is represented in a variety of graphic forms through the medium of comics, which primarily encourage contemplation of the graphic beauty of Japanese writing.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Enseigner la variation en classe de FLE
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Language varies in a multitude of dimensions: regional, social, situational, etc. Based on a large corpus, this article will show that comics contain just a small sample of the variants found in spontaneous speech, where they are not evenly distributed. In comics, regional variants are rare; spoken French variants, on the other hand, such as negation without ne, are commonly found. The use or not of these variants can highlight the contrast between the narrative text in the captions and the spoken word in the speech balloons. They are also often used to stage differences between characters or between the social groups to which they belong (e.g. young people vs. adults). Unlike the external factors (which can be deliberately manipulated), the internal factors of variation (probably unfamiliar to the comic artists) are surprisingly close to spontaneous speech. Which are the didactic consequences of this representation of linguistic variation in comics? This article proposes the use of comics to teach variation in the French as a foreign language classroom, essentially to illustrate the existence of variants. In this context, stereotyped representations may even be an advantage, as they already imply a didactic reduction. However, when complete works are studied in class, teachers must explicitly address the phenomenon of staged orality in writing and make students aware of the fact that variants can be used for stereotyping purposes.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Indigenous Participation: Canada’s Trade for Reconciliation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The constitutional recognition of reconciliation has paved the way for the integration of the Crown’s domestic obligations toward Indigenous peoples into Canada’s international commitments. In this context, trade policy has emerged as an additional avenue through which the national objective of reconciliation may be advanced. This paper examines the incorporation of Indigenous peoples’ rights and interests in six Canadian trade agreements concluded following the launch of Canada’s Progressive Trade Agenda. It analyzes the normative innovations introduced and evaluates the extent to which these agreements move beyond symbolic recognition toward meaningful participation. While the degree of integration varies across agreements, the findings suggest that Canadian trade policy increasingly reflects an effort to align international economic governance with the domestic imperative of reconciliation.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Inclusion or Exclusion of External Voices in Decision-Making on the EU Regulation on Deforestation-Free Products (EUDR): Heard, but Not Listened To
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Over the last years the EU has taken a more unilateral approach in linking sustainable development to trade by adopting legislation that affects the sustainable production and trade of products within and beyond its internal market. One of these laws is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). By many, the adoption of the EUDR has been hailed as a successful linkage between sustainability and trade, and an important step in countering deforestation. Others, however, have criticized the policy making process and the limited possibilities it offered to engage with certain stakeholders and their concerns. Drawing on various theories of the policy process, this article sheds light on processes of exclusion and inclusion during the policymaking process of the EUDR. We show that political opportunity structures mediate the impact of stakeholder mobilization, with their institutional dimensions affecting access to policymakers and their discursive dimensions influencing policymakers' receptiveness to different arguments. We show how exclusion instead of inclusion contributed to stronger or more developed environment-trade linkage in the case of the EUDR.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: From Linkages to Disconnects: The Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Labor provisions in the USMCA, and more specifically its RRM, offer a good case study for this special issue. As a tool for labor rights enforcement, it also is a strategic instrument to realign production away from low-cost production areas. The RRM represents a rare instance of an embedded “trade for” linkage, wherein trade policy is explicitly used as a tool to enforce labor rights. It embodies the kind of linkage that the special issue describes as the strongest form of trade integration, both substantively and procedurally, that ties a trade to social and other non-commercial objectives. However, this article reveals the fragility of trade linkages in a volatile political and strategic context. The re-election of Donald Trump endangers the future of the RRM and the broader social dimension of the USMCA. Trump’s America First doctrine and its deregulatory economic agenda suggest a more disembedded and strategically oriented trade policy. This potential rollback echoes the concept of “trade disconnects,” in which integrated social concerns are de-linked or marginalized when they conflict with nationalist, security-based, or purely commercial imperatives. Yet, the RRM remains an important trade policy instrument and is used by the new administration as a strategic tool to block “social dumping” in North America. This article has four sections: 1) the trade-labor linkage in the literature; 2) the USMCA’s RRM and how it improved the NAFTA side-agreement; 3) the RRM cases and their impacts; and 4) the future of the RRM. As the USMCA approaches its 2026 review, it is crucial to assess the RRM's effectiveness and its future trajectory.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Role of Informality in Shaping Economic Policy Integration
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper examines the relationship between trade linkages, disconnects, and informality in shaping economic policy integration. As global trade undergoes significant transformations due to systemic shocks and structural changes, the informal economy emerges as a crucial yet often overlooked factor in trade policy formulation and analysis. The paper argues that the informal sector plays a critical role in both creating trade disconnects and catalyzing new trade linkages, challenging traditional approaches to trade governance while opening possibilities for innovative policy solutions. The study begins by establishing a conceptual framework that brings together notions of trade linkages, disconnects, and informality. It then explores how informality acts as a source of trade disconnects complicating data analysis, policy enforcement, and market dynamics. Simultaneously, the paper investigates the potential of informal economies to forge unexpected economic connections, particularly in cross-border trade and the digital economy. Examples from African informal trade networks and e-commerce platforms demonstrate this potential. The research then explores the governance implications of these dynamics, emphasizing the need for more inclusive trade policies that can effectively navigate the realities of economies with large informal sectors. It discusses emerging strategies for policy development, such as greater inclusion of informal sector representatives in trade policy formulation and the use of innovative policy instruments that bridge formal and informal economic structures. By bringing together concepts of trade linkages, disconnects, and informality, this research contributes to a more nuanced understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing trade policymakers in the 21st century. It calls for a rethinking of how to approach trade policy formulation and implementation, advocating for new theoretical frameworks and governance models that can balance the dynamism of informal economies with the need for effective regulation and social protection.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Green Virtues of Chinese Protectionism: A Comparative Analysis of EU and US Responses to the China Garbage Shock
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Can economic protectionism in the Global South induce environmental reforms in the Global North? In 2017, China enacted “Operation National Sword,” which banned the import of a subset of internationally traded waste and scrap products. This unexpected and unprecedented collapse in Chinese demand – justified in China on environmental grounds and also an initial move in the brewing US-China trade war – shook global markets. Both the European Union and United States have long relied on exports to achieve “not in my backyard” (NIMBY) waste management goals, and China had become the dominant importer of a variety of their post-industrial and post-consumer products such as waste plastics. Thus, after 2017 EU and US waste exporters had to adjust, by reducing exports and/or diverting to new foreign markets. Conceivably, the collapse in global demand for certain waste products could ripple back to EU and US waste management policy, providing a sufficient shock to advance reform. At the same time, it is well established that the EU has environmental bona fides far exceeding those of the US. We use novel quantitative data to trace the nature of the shock to exports, providing evidence that disruptions to exports manifested in ways more visible to EU audiences than those in the US. Qualitatively, we show that EU-level policy has made meaningful strides, both within the EU and internationally, whereas initially bipartisan US interest frayed, leaving the problem of adjustment to US municipalities. Our analysis departs from conventional policy debates on the links between free trade and the environment to show that protective measures – not just trade agreements – can foster new policy linkages under certain circumstances. As what we term the “China garbage shock” reinforced rather than challenge the preexisting environmental policy cleavage between the EU and US, Chinese protectionism bolstered trade-environment linkages in a most-likely case but did not overcome trade disconnects in a least-likely case.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Plurilateralism within the WTO as a Catalyst for New Trade Linkages: An Analysis of the JSI on E-Commerce
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyzes the potential of the WTO's Joint Initiative on Electronic Commerce (JSI) as a catalyst for fostering e-commerce while meeting sustainable development issues. It explores the challenges of the transition from multilateralism to plurilateralism and traces the genesis of the Joint Initiative on Electronic Commerce. After providing an overview of the provisions of the draft agreement, the article aims to analyze the extent to which development issues have been taken into account by exploring the tensions arising from the negotiations. Inevitably, it identifies the major shortcomings that remain, particularly in terms of environmental sustainability and the inclusion of developing countries. Finally, looking to the future, the article examines the options for integrating this agreement into the WTO legal order.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Furthering Trade and Investment in India’s Healthcare Sector. What Cost to the Public Health Care System?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: India is now the fifth largest global economy thanks to significant growth in exports and international exchange in recent years. The healthcare sector in India is one of the largest and fastest growing in terms of revenue and employment. It is however questionable to what extent increasing trade and investment in the health sector can effectively improve public health care delivery to the population, despite the importance of this critical sector. In line with the trade linkages special issue, this paper questions to what extent trade policy in health services is disembedded from the question of public health care provision. It is important to reiterate that protection of health systems implies engaging in issues beyond the pure economic agenda of countries wishing to further trade and investment. This paper thus takes a social constructivist approach to analyse the impact of the recent increase in trade and investment in the health sector in India. In particular, it draws on Ruggie’s concept of embedded liberalism to explore the potential effects of enhancing international trade and investment in this sector whilst still ensuring that sufficient welfare provisions are in place. It addresses two main questions: can domestic and international regulatory regimes ensure public health systems are protected and what are the trade offs to health care delivery of enhancing trade and investment with international private health care providers.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Environmental Protection in Trade Agreements: A Critical and Constructive View of RCEP
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Trade-Environment linkages have become a prominent phenomenon in contemporary global relations. From being treated as exceptions within the GATT/WTO framework and in earlier regional trade agreements (RTAs), environmental protection has been firmly integrated in multilateral progressive agenda as well as new-generation RTAs as shared obligations rather than as mere acknowledgments of states’ “right to protect”. This evolution demonstrates how trade agreements increasingly contribute to environmental goals. Yet, the recent Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership agreement (RCEP) fails to appropriately address environmental provisions within its framework. This contrasts with the traditional environmental policies of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, at the central of RCEP, as well as with the more progressive approaches adopted by nearly all RCEP members. By tracing the evolution of trade-environment linkages, highlighting selected RTAs concluded by RCEP members, this paper evaluates RCEP’s environmental aspect and offers forward-looking recommendations for more effectively embedding environmental objectives, in line with contemporary trends in sustainable trade governance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Gendered Trade Governance during Covid-19
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The scholarship on trade linkages investigates how trade policy interacts with other policy spheres, such as security, environment, labor or human rights. Recently, this literature has turned towards examining the politics of what is considered to lie “inside” and “outside” of the trade governance arena. Our article offers an engagement with such questions of “trade linkages vs. trade disconnects” from a feminist political economy perspective. We critically analyze the linkages and disconnects between trade and gender, and trade and social reproduction, which is integrally related to the former, in the global trade policy response to the Covid-19 pandemic. We find that global trade policy-makers acknowledged the link between trade and gender during the Covid-19 pandemic and recognized how Covid-19 revealed the insecurities associated with women’s position in productive and reproductive labor. At the same time, our analysis reveals that the Covid-19 trade response also reproduced gender based-inequalities in global trade governance, including the false distinction between production and social reproduction, the privileging of the former above the latter, and the lack of challenges to existing trade rules or orthodoxies, which themselves fuel gender-based inequalities and crises in social reproduction. Overall, we conclude that long-standing disembeddedness and exclusions can be reproduced in the making of new trade linkages, unless the power relations that underpin global trade and global trade governance are actively identified and disturbed.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A propos d’une exposition photographique : Antoni Campañà et la Guerre d’Espagne
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: *This article invites reflection on the relationships between propaganda and photography during the Spanish Civil War. Specifically, it concerns a recent exhibition (Montpellier, June-December 2023) of photographs taken by a Catalan photographer in Barcelona, which were never published or exhibited during the conflict, as the author took care to hide his negatives throughout the Franquist period. While most of the photos were taken from the Republican camp, the last photos show the parade of Franco’s troops in Barcelona. How could the artist reconcile his anarchist sympathies with the ambiguities of the Victory Parade? This is what we aimed to answer through five axes: mobilisation in the face of the coup d'état, icons of the popular response, propaganda, destruction and refugees, victors and vanquished.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: ¿Un anarquismo ‘de ida y vuelta’? La militancia libertaria en Francia como factor de politización y radicalización de la juventud de los sesenta-setenta
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article highlight the role of historical Spanish anarchist militancy in exile in France in the maintenance of a political tradition which, albeit briefly, was recovered in the 1960s and 1970s. In this sense, the spaces generated by this militancy could be experienced by Spaniards who travelled or went into exile at that time as ‘counter-spaces (Foucault, 2010) that led them to acquire or consolidate an anarchist political identity. In this phenomenon, we shouldn’t overlook the role played by revolutionary memory, especially that referring to the Spanish revolution that took place between 1936-1937 in the Republican rearguard of the Civil War. The transnational element is thus shown to be a factor to be considered in analyses that focus on the trajectory of radical activism in the 1960s and 1970s. Finally, Black's life story serves to analyse all this through a concrete experience.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The aim of this article is to analyse the case of the Spaniards who fought as volunteers in the French Foreign Legion during the First World War. In the Spanish case, within the framework of an extraordinarily intense cultural mobilisation, there was a twofold nationalist instrumentalisation: in a Catalanist sense, with the hope of exporting Catalan claims to sovereignty, and in a reactive Spanishist sense. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Cartas transpirenaicas. Usos, problemas y reapropiaciones de la correspondencia entre España y Francia en el marco de la guerrilla antifranquista
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The relationship between the anti-Francoist guerrillas and France was very close. A large number of PCE cadres with experience in the French Resistance left France to join the ranks of the guerrilla groups fighting the dictatorship. In the same way, crossing the Pyrenees was the main way to put an end to their struggle and be able to start a new life without the constant persecution of the dictatorship's repression. In both contexts, letters were a daily companion to unite these fighters with their families who remained in Spain. Sending and receiving letters was an emotional relief for these partisans, but it also involved significant risks and complex relationships. In this article we will explore the issues linked to these practices produced by the cross-border postal exchange between guerrillas and their loved ones.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Una red transnacional tejida en las ondas. Las emisiones de «Radio París» en el espacio transfronterizo franco-español (1960-1973)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: At the end of the 1950s, Spanish economic emigration attracted the attention of Radio Paris, which, faced with the explosion of this phenomenon, became a social actor linked to the migratory dynamics themselves. In this way, its communicative functions went beyond mere information and contributed to the construction of a transnational communication network. This paper examines the capacity of radio to generate these social and cultural fields between one country and another. It also aims to examine the relationship established between the listeners in Spain and those displaced on French soil and the radio station, in order to analyse, on the one hand, the impact of its content. On the other hand, we will focus on highlighting, from a gender perspective, the differences expressed by women in their use of the radio medium.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La medicina española en el espejo de Francia (1820-1860). Modelos, intercambios, tensiones
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyses the relationship and transfers in the field of medicine between France and Spain during the core decades of the nineteenth century. These relationships, almost always asymmetrical due to the higher consideration of the French medicine in the world, allow us to better understand the debates on medical science and profession in both empires. Our main sources are Spanish medical press as well as those Spanish medical treatises that were read and translated in France. We also examine professional trajectories of Spanish physicians linked to France in one way or another. Overall, analysing the contacts between French and Spanish medicine between 1820 and 1860 shows the different position of both countries within the transimperial medical community in Europe and America. French medicine became an aspirational model for the Spanish; however, g the dialogue and discussion with and the criticisms of the French physicians, medical science and institutions became a symbolic battlefield on which the Spanish physicians fought their internal professional conflicts. The references to France also served to legitimize the Spanish physicians’ collective projects and their strategies aimed at boosting their political influence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Late Bronze Age Metal Artefact Hoard at Barraca, Saint-Victor-la-Coste (Gard)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In 2018, a hoard of bronze artefacts was discovered by chance during agricultural work at the Barraca site in Saint-Victor-la-Coste (Gard). A test excavation was carried out to identify the original location of the hoard and to collect other artefacts, resulting in the discovery of 42 mostly fragmentary metal objects belonging to various functional categories (weapons, ornaments, tools, foundry waste). The typological diversity of the objects points to several regions of influence (Alps, Massif Central, Pyrenees, Germany), whereas the metallurgical homogeneity suggests local production. However, isotopic analyses indicate that the copper used to make the objects came from the south-eastern Alps (Trentino-Alto Adige). This copper appears to have been brought to the south of France in the form of pick ingots, fragments of which are present in the deposit. Located at the interface between the spheres of influence of two ceramic styles (Rhine-Switzerland-Eastern France and the southern fringes of the Massif Central), this hoard illustrates the role of the Lower Rhône Valley as a cultural crossroads during the Late Bronze Age.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Assessing the potential transition of Lake Titicaca to a terminal lake
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Lake Titicaca in South America is highly sensitive to climatic variability, making it particularly vulnerable to climate change and raising concerns about long-term drying. Fluctuations in lake-water-levels (LWLs) can trigger cascading impacts across the downstream Titicaca-Desaguadero-Poopó-Salares (TDPS). This study evaluates the dependence of Lake Titicaca’s water level on air temperature and precipitation using a rainfall-runoff model to estimate river inflows, combined with a lake routing model (LRM) to simulate water-level variations. Future projections of LWLs were developed using extreme precipitation and evaporation rates and downscaled climate scenarios, from which temperature trend were incorporated into the LWLs modeling. Results suggested that, even with no significant changes in precipitation, a continued increase in evaporation of approximately 3 mm per year associated with rising air temperatures in the whole catchment could cause Lake Titicaca to become a terminal lake by around 2050 and permanently terminal lake after 2085. A decrease in precipitation or further increases in evaporation would likely accelerate this transition due to the reduction in lake surface area. Such changes could have major consequences for the TDPS system and increase the likelihood that Lake Poopó becomes permanently dried-up.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La nascita della tragedia dallo spirito di Aristotele. Una lettura aristotelica della poetica di Nietzsche
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Nietzsche’s theory in The Birth of Tragedy is traditionally considered as opposed to Aristotle’s Poetics. The essay aims to show that there are some genuinely Aristotelian elements underlying Nietzsche’s account of tragedy. I will first argue that Nietzsche’s own criticism of Aristotle is directed at an unattractive reading of the concept of katharsis. After providing an updated interpretation of Aristotle’s account, I will argue that two of its pivotal elements are also at the core of Nietzsche’s view: 1) the explanation of the sympathetic identification with the tragic hero; 2) the account of the effects of the tragedy on the attendants. I maintain that both the accounts underline the importance of the undeserveness of the hero’s sufferings, in order to pity them; and that, for both Aristotle and Nietzsche, tragedy allows us to grasp some universally painful traits of human existence, while teaching us to confront them with joy.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’artificio dell’individuo sovrano. L’individuale e la legge come problemi estetici
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The contribution offers a critical interpretation of the notion of the “sovereign individual” – which Nietzsche presents in the second paragraph of the second dissertation of The Genealogy of Morals – based on its interconnection with aesthetic concepts and issues. In the first part, it argues for the compatibility between a positive reading of this figure and a parodic one by highlighting Nietzsche’s ironic use of Kantian terminology in opposition to Edward von Hartmann. In doing so, the article also clarifies Nietzsche’s critique of Kant’s notion of autonomy. It then shows how an interpretation through aesthetic categories opens up new hermeneutic perspectives that, on the one hand, connect moral, political, and aesthetic issues in Nietzsche’s philosophical work, and, on the other, underscore Nietzsche’s historical-philosophical relevance within modernity. In particular, the author demonstrates how the idea of “individual law,” implied by Nietzsche’s reference to the sovereign individual, is analogous to reflective aesthetic judgments, whose “principle of determination can only be subjective.” Finally, the contribution explores the implications of Nietzsche’s aesthetic understanding of moral autonomy for the modern notion of sovereignty.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Becoming New in Old Age. Bodily Experience and Personal Flourishing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper aims at investigating ageing as a multifaceted experience in which a redefinition of one’s habitualities of experience, which often comes with a reduction of previous possibilities and a stronger sense of one’s finitude and vulnerability, can still coexist with moments of personal flourishing. I will particularly examine the bodily dimension of ageing, analyzing how one’s body feels in old age and what valences the new experiences of one’s body have for the older person. I will then argue that, despite the fact that the older person’s body often undergoes a physical decline, one’s possible personal flourishing in old age does not exclude the bodily dimension, but can reverberate positively in it, giving room to bright new experiences of one’s embodied personal life.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Nuove capacità e nuove qualità. Due forme diverse, ma complementari, di novità ontologica
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Intuitively, what is (ontologically) new differs from everything else and begins to exist at a certain moment in time. An entity is new if it is different from the rest and unprecedented from before. A genuinely new phenomenon can appear when created “from nothing” by a God, when produced by an intentional agent, or when spontaneously emerging from more elementary components. This paper focuses on these last cases, which involve “emergent novelty”. Following the debate about emergence, two interpretations of ontological novelty can be identified: the first one is causal, while the second one can be defined as “qualitative”. The former, prevalent in contemporary philosophical discourse, equates ontological novelty with the emergence of new causal properties such as tendencies, capacities or powers. According to the latter, novelty corresponds to the appearance of new qualities – i.e., properties that do not seem essentially or merely causal. This paper seeks to clarify the latter view by identifying the type of properties involved in qualitative novelty. Furthermore, it advocates integrating the causal and qualitative perspectives to develop a more comprehensive criterion for understanding ontological novelty.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: What Is the “New”?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: What is the new? Deleuze frequently said that the question of the conditions for the production of the new – or novelty (Whitehead) or creativity (Bergson) – was one of the fundamental questions of contemporary thought. In this article, we distinguish the problem of new from a number of related but distinct problems, such as questions of transformation and change, causality, and emergence. Deleuze’s claim is that novelty (difference) must become a fundamental concept at the most basic ontological level (Being = the new = difference). We ask what the conditions for the production of the new might be, and argue that such conditions must be differential through and through, where difference is related to difference through difference itself.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The (Old) Myth of Dematerialization and Its Overestimation in Contemporary Arts
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Dematerialization was pivotal for the spread of new artistic practices since the 60s and 70s as well as for the theoretical debate concerning the renewal of contemporary arts. What we usually call ‘dematerialization’ could be considered a long-standing myth invoked to highlight our role as producers of thought. This narrative is determined by an overestimation, that is, by what we could describe as a substitution of fetishes: the fetishized commodity (the reference to the material bodies of works of art and bulwark of the modernist discourse on the arts) is replaced by the fetishized thought (the reference to the immaterial nature of the works and cornerstone of the contemporary discourse on the arts and their transformations today). In the critical discourse about the arts, every time the thesis of dematerialization is defended, this substitution takes place with the primary motive being the attempt to give importance not so much to what we do – since that would already imply a materialist inclination – but, above all, to what we think and say. In this essay, after having illustrated the assumptions and the theme of dematerialization, I evaluate the hypothesis of overestimation and some of its consequences on our ways to explain novelty in the arts.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Webfare for Social Wellbeing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In the digital age, data has become a powerful and renewable form of capital, yet its benefits remain concentrated among corporations and state actors. This paper aims to present Webfare as a transformative model that redistributes data wealth, prioritising ethical, equitable, and sustainable use for societal wellbeing.This framework empowers individuals, institutions, and communities to reclaim, manage, and capitalise on their data assets, moving beyond traditional welfare models. By integrating data cooperatives, synthetic data generation, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, Webfare ensures privacy, fairness, and responsible AI deployment. It promotes a circular data economy, where data is not just a tool for private profit but a public good, reinvested into social progress.Ultimately, Webfare redefines data ownership and AI’s role in society, fostering economic efficiency, social equity, ethical governance, and democratic empowerment – building a future where data serves the many, not just the few.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Transformative Virtue of Surprise in Politics
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In what follows, I will focus on the opposite of the top-down, “transcendent” politics of surprise, institutional and instituted, in short, remote-controlled. I’m more interested in the immanent dynamic of the “we” (first person plural) that “makes” the political surprise, and how the social forces of the human collective, of the political community in the deepest sense of civil, civic and citizen society, not only produce and construct, but also feed off such a dynamic.I will first draw on Gilles Deleuze’s approach and show how political surprise can be understood as a process characterized by intensification, with the reaching of a critical threshold, followed by a period of saturation (my three phases in the model of surprise). The presentation of this first model will lead me to explore its limits, particularly in view of the quantified, objectifying negative vision of surprise that it illustrates. I will then propose another alternative model, characterized by its dynamic of openness and the creation of new possibilities. This dynamic, as we shall see, places the individual at the service of the collective intersubjective interactions, without absorbing them, as long as the individual keeps the ability for a renewed examination of his or her assumed mode of alignment with collective creation. The creation of a new collective results then the creation of a “we” co-acted by and within each individual.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: How Can AI Help Us? Tecnologia e destino: dalla metafisica alla rivoluzione digitale
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The essay discusses the theoretical aspect of the relationship between natural intelligence and AI. The former, embedded in a body, capable of empathy, feelings, emotions, subject to opaque and obscure determinations due to sensitivity, is subordinate to artificial intelligence, which instead can vastly exceed human capabilities. On the other hand, human beings, however much they may perceive their own inadequacy compared to automata – unlike tools potentially designed to last indefinitely – can decide, and program, their own death. After discussing philosophical positions concerning artificial intelligence, the focus shifts to the debate between those who mark the difference between the two intelligences through an ad hoc faculty, understanding, and those who, like Ferraris, counter that this difference does not reveal the qualitative diversity between natural intelligence and artificial intelligence. Rather, the dissonance lies primarily not on the level of understanding, but on that of purpose, and therefore on reason as the capacity to manifest aims, to have final causes, to confer meanings. The conclusion considers the relationship between natural intelligence and AI from the intersection of critical theory, digital studies and philosophy of mind.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Tecnologia e capitale nel lavoro di Maurizio Ferraris. Al di là della metafisica quantitativa
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In questo saggio propongo una riflessione sul concetto di capitalizzazione nella filosofia documediale di Maurizio Ferraris. Analizzando i concetti principali della sua metafisica della registrazione, sostengo che la nozione di capitalizzazione, benché intesa ad aiutarci a capire il processo di ominizzazione e la non-essenza umana, rischia di sottometterli all’imperativo dell’accumulazione indifferente, in linea con un’interpretazione quantitativa del rapporto fra l’umanità e i suoi supplementi o tecnologie. Il risultato, a mio avviso, è che certi aspetti della metafisica di Ferraris, e in particolare la figura dell’anima-automa, nascano più dalla logica dell’attuale sistema socioeconomico e tecnologico che da un’ontologia. Concludo suggerendo che un’altra nozione da lui proposta, la responsività, possa offrire una chiave più dialettica per sviluppare un’analisi dell’essere umano, in quanto “animale disadattato”, nel suo rapporto con la tecnologia.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Dalla selce al digitale. Traiettorie filogenetiche e ontogenetiche della mente tecnico-simbolica
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article investigates the role of technology in the phylogenesis and ontogenesis of the human mind, focusing on technical-symbolic capacity as both an evolutionary driver and a key to understanding contemporary subjectivity. From an extended evolutionary perspective, technology is not merely a tool but a cognitive and cultural environment that shapes neurocognitive, emotional, and social transformations. The paper retraces the major stages of technical evolution – from Oldowan flakes to digital devices – showing how each technological transition has reconfigured the human mind. In ontogenetic terms, technology emerges as a semiotic environment that structures learning, symbolization, and self-construction. The psychopathological implications of digital cognitive environments are examined in light of neuroplasticity, predictive processing, and evolutionary mismatch. A critical discussion is offered on the concept of the ‘augmented mind’, highlighting the tensions between enhancement and alienation, extension and identity fragmentation. Finally, the therapeutic potential of technology is explored, with reference to virtual reality, artificial intelligence, and telepsychiatry. This contribution aims to outline the contours of a psychology of the technical mind that integrates anthropology, psychopathology, and evolutionary theory.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Human Because of Technology (Yet, Myself Because of Me)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: What we learn even from ancient Western culture is that humans are definitely human because of technology as what distinguishes them most. Thus, what we should ask ourselves as philosophers is not if we are human because of technology, but to what extent our human identity coincides with our technological capability and, if they do not coincide, to what extent the latter can exceed at least partly the former.As a case in point, I propose to use something extreme, i.e. our attempt to technologically defeat our death: several biotechnology companies and publications share the objective of not dying. The basic idea is to think of death not as a metaphysical issue, but as an engineering problem, which, precisely as an engineering problem, can be (technologically) solved. But, even though it is true that being human means having the constitutive drive to transcend one’s own being human, and that human technological capability is the most used to do it, the question is if we have alternative ways of transcending our own being human that may even be more valuable than our technological capability to engineer death. I will argue in the affirmative by proposing to think of our capability to face our death by being existentially responsible for it as essential for the definition of our identity. In other words, I will argue that human identity can exceed technological capability – which means that humans, both individually and socially, can, and even should, decide to what extent the former can exceed the latter, especially at a time when the primary objective of technology seems to be the defeat of ageing and death as the removal of time from human identity.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Da Homo technologicus a Homo naturans? Nietzsche e il futuro dell’etica
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Maurizio Ferraris shows a recurrent skepticism toward moral philosophy, often criticizing its limiting and moralistic tendencies. Yet his work, particularly from the phase of New Realism onward, reveals a growing ethical dimension, culminating in the idea of ‘webfare’. This apparent ambivalence is here clarified through a Nietzschean lens: Ferraris’ rejection of moral normativity aligns with Nietzsche’s genealogical critique, while his ethical tension reflects a constructive will to create. This positive and creative form of ethics has its roots in an anthropology that sees the human being as a not yet determined being. In this diagnosis that he shares with Nietzsche, Ferraris sees in technology the distinctive character of the human being (that we can describe indeed as Homo technologicus), but this perspective leads to an anthropocentric vision of ethics, which could be extended by developing Nietzsche’s theses in the direction of Homo naturans. According with this form of anthropology, ethics arises from active participation in a broader natural process, and becomes a creative act of meaning-making, grounded not in transcendent truths but in human responsibility and natural interdependence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Memory, the Pocket Book, and the Hard Core of the Consciousness
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While scholars across several disciplines contend that human evolution proceeds along an inexorable trajectory – furtherly accelerated by technological innovation and thus establishing analogies between biological and technological advancement – literature has long articulated a latent anxiety regarding the rise of mechanization. The works of Samuel Butler, E.M. Forster, H.G. Wells, A. Huxley and G. Orwell stand for paradigmatic expressions of such a cultural apprehension. During the twentieth century, intellectuals from diverse domains examined the role of media – conceived by Marshall McLuhan as an extension of human faculties – and electronic technology, as theorized by Günther Anders, in shaping and conditioning subjectivity. In the face of scenarios often represented in stark, dystopian tones, one final redoubt appears to preserve the irreducible specificity of the human domain vis-à-vis with not only machines, but also increasingly Artificial Intelligence: namely, consciousness. This consideration recalls a fundamental epistemological inquiry: can consciousness legitimately be regarded as synonymous with intelligence?

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper introduces the 90th issue of “Rivista di estetica”, which examines the distinctive bond between human beings and technology. Building on Ferraris’s claim that technological revolutions shape humanity because humans are defined by their relation to technics, the contributions included in this issue investigate the constitutive role of technology in human life, especially in light of the transformations brought by the Web and Artificial Intelligence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Gudrun Corvinus’ Personal and Scientific Experiences in the International Afar Research Expedition, Ethiopia, 1973-1975
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In the years 2024 and 2025, the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle in Paris received a collection of more than 1,000 written documents and photographs collected by Gudrun Corvinus between 1973 and 1975, when she was a member of the International Afar Research Expedition (1972-1977). During these expeditions, major fossils were discovered, including the iconic “Lucy” (Australopithecus afarensis) and what until recently were the oldest stone tools. While Corvinus focused on Pleistocene deposits of the Afar region, she additionally illustrated and described her experiences in letters and journal entries, and with photographs. This paper presents these archives and demonstrates how they can be used to encompass various research themes that contribute to an historiography of palaeoanthropology in eastern Africa. It includes fieldwork practices, the context of fossil discovery and collection, and the Western appropriation of scientific narratives about Africa’s past, as well as the history of scientific cooperation between the West and eastern Africa within the broader postcolonial continental context.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Remapping the Senegambian megaliths: Beyond the culture area paradigm
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Between 1969 and 1982, Victor Martin and Charles Becker led a series of reconnaissance missions to document thousands of sites for their Inventaire des Sites Protohistoriques de la Sénégambie. This dataset has since become a cornerstone in the archaeology of central Senegambia, where site distribution maps continue to define a “Megalith Zone” and provide context for excavations at well-known type-sites. However, we argue that spatial and quantitative data from the Inventaire can do more to help us envision megalithic sites as places embedded in complex social landscapes. We begin by exploring how the Inventaire emerged from and now perpetuates a culture area paradigm through mapping strategies of selection and simplification. We then advocate for a more relational paradigm in Senegambian archaeology by developing a critical cartography of megalithic sites recently digitized for MAEASaM (Mapping Africa’s Endangered Archaeological Sites and Monuments). Here we use recent survey results and geostatistical tools to assess and visualize uncertainties in the Inventaire, while also working to better illustrate megalithic monuments as material expressions of social interaction at multiple scales. In so doing, we emphasize how fresh approaches to “legacy” data from the Inventaire and similar spatial archives could aid with efforts to decolonize African archaeology.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Mehlman archives and the archaeology of Nasera rockshelter, Tanzania
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Archives are increasingly recognized as a critical element in archaeological research in eastern Africa and elsewhere that, unlike excavation, are a non-destructive source of information. However, the utility of any archive is dependent in part on its availability. We report here on the recent recovery of the archives of Michael J. Mehlman, who excavated at multiple important archaeological sites in northern Tanzania. Establishing clear plans for preservation, documentation, and data sharing are underway. In this article, archive materials from Mehlman’s work at the Middle and Later Stone Age site of Nasera rockshelter provide a starting point to assess the collection and its research potential and to gain a better understanding of the 1975–1976 excavations. Like other sites in eastern Africa, archaeological investigations at Nasera follow an approximate 42-year research cycle, emphasizing the need to preserve this collection and those that follow from it for future scholarly generations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Reopening the archives of archaeology at Ile-Ife, Nigeria: Towards a history of the Osangangan Obamakin sacred grove
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In 1953, the archaeologists Bernard Fagg and A.J.H. Goodwin excavated sacred grove sites in Ile-Ife, south-western Nigeria, where they hoped to uncover artefactual and stratigraphic evidence of the town’s early history. They were especially interested in developing artefact typologies and chronologies, as part of the systematisation of archaeology in Africa during this period. But far from primordial places conserving undisturbed records of past human practices, such sacred groves were dynamic spaces with complex histories where successive communities repeatedly remodified and reinterpreted earlier cultural features and their larger landscape. This article revisits the excavations of the grove of Osangangan Obamakin, drawing upon the largely unpublished records to address new questions about the grove’s early and recent past, and the significance of its archaeology to understanding the wider history of Ife’s cultural landscapes.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Towards the creation of archaeological archives in Ghana: Reflections from Begho
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Begho, an ancient market town located in Ghana, was the focus of archaeological and ethnographic research in the 1970s due to its past trade links with Jenne in the Niger Bend. While much work has been done at Begho, not much is known about the archaeological practice that was carried out at the site. It is against this backdrop that the current research was conducted. This study assessed and examined archival documents of previous researchers who worked at Begho, to identify and interrogate Begho artefacts at the Museum of Archaeology, University of Ghana. It further examined field notes, site plans, maps, illustrations, and photographs from Begho in the 1970s. Based on the archival data source, a search and analysis of Begho cultural materials kept in the museum storages were undertaken. The research provides insights into the reconstruction of an archaeological site by using archival records and museum artefacts, which are key components in the creation of an archaeological archives/repository. This study derives its significance from the fact that it would contribute to the creation of an archaeological archives/repository.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les fouilles suisses à Tabo (1965-1974). Plongée dans la mémoire archivistique d’une mission archéologique au Soudan
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The site of Tabo, the occupation of which spans from the 2nd millennium BCE to the Medieval (Christian) period, is in northern Sudan. It was excavated between 1965 and 1974 by a mission from the University of Geneva. The results of these archaeological investigations remain largely unpublished. This article provides an overview of the ongoing study of the archives and materials from these excavations. This project is the result of collaboration between the following institutions:- the Swiss-French-Sudanese Archaeological Mission of Kerma-Doukki Gel, which inherited the scientific intellectual property of Charles Bonnet’s works;- the Museum of Art and History in Geneva, where the artefacts from Tabo are housed; - the Natural History Museum of Geneva, which preserves the archaeozoological material; the University of Geneva, with the ARCAN laboratory (Faculty of Sciences), where the anthropological remains and documentary archives are stored; the Egyptology Unit (Faculty of Arts), which holds documents from the archives of Helen Jacquet-Gordon and Jean Jacquet.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Chantiers d’histoire : enquêtes sur les archives de l’archéologie africaine
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article introduces a thematic issue focused on the archives of African archaeology. Produced during field operations that are often irreversible, these archives—including notes, drawings, photographs, correspondence, and artefact collections – constitute the primary, and sometimes sole, record of excavated contexts. Although fragmentary and dispersed among public institutions and private collections far beyond the continent’s borders and further compromised by institutional discontinuities stemming from the colonial period, they nonetheless represent essential resources for the writing of African history. A critical reading of these materials enables scholars to challenge historiographical narratives that have often been reproduced without sufficient scrutiny, in the absence of alternative sources. This process reveals gaps and silences, including invisible actors, concealed practices, and interpretations anchored in now-outdated paradigms. Revisiting earlier excavations, reconstructing archaeological practices, re-examining collections, and reassessing the evidentiary record are integral to an approach that seeks to reconstruct, fragment by fragment, what has been scattered by time and neglect. The objective is not to indict previous researchers, but to reopen “cold cases” and to engage them with questions and interpretive frameworks of the present. Beyond presenting the contributions gathered in this special issue and surveying the current challenges posed by the use of African archaeological archives, this article examines four collections relating to southwestern Nigeria. Their contrasting documentary trajectories illustrate both the heterogeneity of such corpora and the fragility of the connections through which they can be traced.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The National Museum of Jos as an Archaeological Archive: A Model for Museum-Based Research in sub-Saharan Africa
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article set out to address a methodological challenge that has become increasingly urgent for African archaeology: how can the archives of archaeology, including collections of artefacts, field documentation, registers, and ‘grey literature’, be mobilised not merely for purposes of heritage inventory and disciplinary historiography, but as first-hand sources of archaeological data capable of producing renewed historical knowledge of past African societies? The case of the National Museum of Jos demonstrates both the necessity and the difficulty of such a project. We argue that the Jos archive must therefore be treated as a layered corpus, shaped by successive regimes of data production and governance. The resulting archival ecology has been hybrid and fragmented. Yet fragmentation, as shown here, does not prevent archival archaeology; it defines the conditions under which archaeological knowledge can be responsibly reconstructed from ‘legacy data’.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Exploring INQF-Based Curriculum in English Education Study Programs: Investigation of Curriculum Implementation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study is about implementing the higher education curriculum based on the Indonesian National Qualification Framework (INQF). It was done at Universitas Kristen Indonesia strictly in the English Language Education Study Program. This study aims to find out how the implementation of the higher education curriculum based on INQF is. The study method used was a qualitative study with a descriptive design. The data of the study were collected through interviews. The instrument of the study was the interview sheet. The informants of the study were the head of the Quality Assurance Agency of Universitas Kristen Indonesia, the head of the Faculty Quality Assurance Agency, and the lecturers of the English Language Education Study Program. The data taken through interviews were analyzed descriptively through transcribing the interview data, data reduction, data display, and drawing conclusions. The result of the study is that the implementation of the learned curriculum is found to be through applicable, simple, and appropriate syllabus content, adding new information, and achieving goals and objectives, according to curriculum planning and quality standards. However, it requires improvement in certain parts of the curriculum implementation that some of the lecturers did not adjust the INQF-Based curriculum into the course they taught. Then it is concluded that although the INQF-Based curriculum has been structurally and well organized, it needs to be implemented by the whole lecturers in their learning and teaching. These findings suggest to the leadership of the University through the Quality Assurance Agency to control the implementation of the curriculum both at the Study Program level and at the lecturer level in carrying out the teaching and learning process.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Impacts des systèmes alimentaires territoriaux sur la biodiversité et stratégies de conservation : une recension des écrits
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Local Food Systems (LFS) refer to an approach to managing food system locally, often emphasizing the development of a sustainable agricultural and agri-food sector, food security, justice and equity, Indigenous food sovereignty, intersectoral governance, and ecosystem preservation. This study aimed to document the complex interactions between LFS and biodiversity issues, as well as potential conservation strategies. A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines using the Web of Science, CAB Abstracts, and Google Scholar databases, resulting in the analysis of 40 publications. The results indicate that biodiversity plays a key role in pollination, biological control, and soil fertility. Its degradation leads to a decline in ecosystem services, reduced agricultural productivity, and the scarcity of traditional foods, particularly affecting Indigenous communities. Practices within LFS can negatively impact biodiversity by causing habitat destruction, land degradation due to intensive farming practices, and a reduction in crop diversity. However, LFS can also contribute to biodiversity conservation by promoting agricultural biodiversity, enhancing ecosystem services, and supporting the development of agroecological practices. Finally, several conservation strategies have been identified, including promoting agroecology, managing habitats and protected areas, and integrating biodiversity concerns into agricultural policies.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La géo-participation des usagers-habitants : réflexions sur une opportunité et une perspective pour un monitorage des territoires urbains
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the conditions for implementing a collaborative (geo)monitoring system aimed at supporting territorial management and enhancing urban resilience. Drawing on GeoWeb technologies and crowdsourcing practices, it proposes a conceptual framework based on a systemic analysis of communication within the territorial actors’ subsystem - particularly residents and managers - to enhance the in situ flow of information and improve technical processes (urban planning, sanitation, waste management, transportation, etc.). The implementation in the Lamkansa neighborhood of Casablanca illustrates the relevance of this approach, where resident users can report environmental anomalies (e.g., household waste) through a dedicated mobile application, thereby fostering more responsive collaboration and improved local management. However, the study identifies several constraints that must be addressed, including the digital divide, the complexity of geo-participatory tools, disparities in stakeholders’ objectives, and the opacity of decision-making processes. In response, a set of recommendations is proposed, including interface simplification, ethical data use, greater transparency in governance, and the involvement of residents from the earliest stages of tool design. Beyond this implementation, the article advances a methodological reflection on the role of participatory data in decision-support processes, drawing on the frameworks of policy analytics, procedural rationality, and instrumented citizenship. The motivations and implications of such a methodological reflection are discussed. So the article highlights the potential of collaborative (geo)monitoring to renew governance practices, enrich territorial knowledge, and strengthen urban resilience through collective intelligence.
