oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Large-scale molecular epidemiological survey of Giardia and Cryptosporidium in Victoria, Australia (2020–2024), reveals novel subtypes and outbreak-associated lineages
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: ABSTRACT Cryptosporidium and Giardia are major causes of gastrointestinal illness globally. In Australia, cryptosporidiosis is nationally notifiable, yet molecular characterization is not routinely undertaken, limiting outbreak detection, source attribution, and zoonotic risk assessment. This limitation became apparent in 2024, when Australia experienced a 273% increase in cryptosporidiosis notifications, the third-highest rise globally. We conducted a molecular epidemiological investigation of Cryptosporidium and Giardia in fecal samples from humans with gastroenteritis in Victoria, Australia, between 2020 and 2024. Positive samples were sequenced using SSU and gp60 for Cryptosporidium and tpi for Giardia, and parasite load was estimated. Of the 2,330 samples tested, 225 were positive for Cryptosporidium and nine for Giardia. One Giardia sample was identified as sub-assemblage AI, two as AII, and six as assemblage B. Seven Cryptosporidium species and 24 subtypes were identified, including eight novel subtypes. Cryptosporidium hominis predominated (85%), followed by C. parvum and C. meleagridis. Six C. hominis subtypes were detected, three associated with 11 recreational water-linked outbreaks in 2024. Subtypes IaA12R3 and IeA11G3T3 were most frequent, in line with global trends; concordance analysis indicated that at least 52 additional cases were likely linked to outbreaks. Several C. parvum subtypes were identified, including two linked to childcare and camp outbreaks. Novel human-infective subtypes of C. occultus, C. fayeri, and C. meleagridis were also detected. These findings reveal extensive Cryptosporidium diversity in Victoria and highlight the value of molecular surveillance for resolving transmission pathways and informing public health responses.IMPORTANCECryptosporidium is a nationally notifiable pathogen in Australia, yet routine subtyping is not performed, limiting the detection of both outbreak-related and sporadic transmission and constraining source attribution. This study represents the first large-scale molecular surveillance of human Cryptosporidium and Giardia infections in southern Australia, including the first molecular epidemiological exploration of the marked increase in cryptosporidiosis observed in 2024. By integrating species, subtype, or assemblage information with epidemiological metadata, we demonstrate substantial Cryptosporidium lineage diversity in symptomatic patients, including multiple novel subtypes and zoonotic transmission. These findings demonstrate the critical value of molecular tools for uncovering hidden transmission, resolving pathways contributing to both sporadic disease and outbreak, and informing targeted public health responses. The findings provide a strong foundation for incorporating routine genotyping into national surveillance systems for parasitic eukaryotic enteropathogens, and the accompanying international comparison of case trends suggests broader transmission dynamics of significant public health relevance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Development of a broad-lineage Lassa virus rapid diagnostic test informed by the WHO REASSURED framework
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: ABSTRACT Lassa fever is a high-risk viral disease endemic to West Africa for which rapid and reliable diagnosis is essential for outbreak control. Here, we describe the development of a lateral flow-based rapid diagnostic test (RDT) targeting the Lassa virus nucleoprotein using newly generated monoclonal antibody pairs. The analytical performance of the assay was evaluated using human serum and plasma specimens as well as inactivated Lassa virus strains and compared with a commercially available antigen test. The final RDT (Pair 2; 1P-44-7/9B-28) demonstrated high analytical sensitivity and 100% specificity across 60 human samples and detected multiple genetically diverse Lassa virus strains, with lineage-dependent differences in analytical sensitivity. In direct analytical comparisons using recombinant antigen, the assay was approximately 64-fold more sensitive than the ReLASV Pan-Lassa Antigen Rapid Test. The RDT provides a rapid visual readout, remains stable at ambient temperatures, and is suitable for decentralized testing workflows, features aligned with key aspects of the World Health Organization (WHO) REASSURED framework. These results indicate that the developed RDT offers a robust and broadly reactive platform for Lassa virus antigen detection and has potential utility for surveillance and outbreak response in resource-limited settings.IMPORTANCELassa fever remains a significant public health concern in West Africa, where diagnostic capacity is often limited in endemic regions. This study describes the development of a broad-lineage Lassa virus rapid diagnostic test informed by the World Health Organization (WHO) REASSURED framework. The assay demonstrates high analytical sensitivity and broad lineage coverage in a field-deployable format, supporting its potential utility for early case detection and decentralized surveillance in endemic settings.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Contribution of Organizational Culture in Schools to Improving Teacher Performance
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The role of organizational culture in improving school quality cannot be ignored, such as hard work habits, responsibility, relationships between school members, and efforts to improve quality. Meanwhile, teacher performance is very important for academic achievement. This study aims to reveal the extent of the role of organizational culture in schools in improving teacher performance. The approach used in this study is qualitative by using the narrative literature review method. The results of this study indicate that the role of organizational culture on teacher performance is very large. However, the implementation of organizational culture faces various obstacles, such as the socialization of regulations that have not been maximized, teachers who have not been disciplined, and in general, school residents who are comfortable with their previous habits. The influence of organizational culture on teacher performance and teacher motivation is quite significant. What needs to be anticipated are the implications because organizational culture that has been embedded for a long time sometimes becomes an obstacle to the change process.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Dominance of forest structural traits in shaping soil bacterial community assembly in Beijing’s urban forests
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Urban forests constitute vital ecological interfaces between built environments and natural systems, yet the mechanisms driving soil microbial community assembly in these ecosystems remain poorly understood. Through an integrated analysis of five dominant forest types (Populus tomentosa, Salix matsudana, Robinia pseudoacacia, Eucommia ulmoides, and Ailanthus altissima) in Beijing’s plain ecological forests, we reveal hierarchical environmental controls over bacterial diversity and network structure. High-throughput sequencing and co-occurrence network analyses demonstrated that Salix matsudana forest harbored the highest microbial diversity (Shannon index = 5.82 ± 0.14), with Proteobacteria abundance significantly elevated compared to other forest types (P < 0.01). Structural equation modeling (SEM) identified soil total nitrogen (TN) as the principal direct suppressor of bacterial diversity (path coefficient = -0.33, P < 0.001), while forest structural traits—particularly diameter at breast height—emerged as critical mediators of community composition through nutrient modulation (R² = 0.502). Notably, microbial networks exhibited forest-type-specific topologies: Populus tomentosa forest stands showed exceptional connectivity (edge density = 0.29), whereas Robinia pseudoacacia forest developed modular architectures (modularity = 2.30) enhancing ecological resilience. These findings establish a mechanistic framework linking forest management practices to microbial-mediated ecosystem functions, with direct implications for urban green space optimization under accelerating anthropogenic pressures.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La transformation du travail de conseil en séjour touristique au prisme des données : résistances et opportunités
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In 2017, the French government launched “DataTourisme”, a platform designed to aggregate territorial tourism data and make it available to foster innovation and new digital uses in the tourism sector. This initiative serves as a lever for a public policy of open data, extending and deepening the ongoing digital transformation. Within this framework, the issue of ‘data quality’ has become increasingly decisive in meeting the challenges of data usability and the expectations of transformation at the heart of the open data movement. However, eight years later, the heterogeneous quality of this data continues to limit its full mobilisation. What are the causes of this heterogeneous quality? By closely examining the data producers, analyzing the tensions embedded in professional data entry practices, and tracing the data collection process—through an ethnographic study conducted in a tourist office—this research seeks to identify the obstacles hindering the promise of efficient open data and its potential to support tourism development.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La politique des statistiques internationales du tourisme : entre exigences financières et préoccupations environnementales
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: With data-sharing platforms, such as Airbnb or Booking.com, tourism has experienced a new boom, barely delayed by the Covid-19 health crisis, which has sparked a resurgence of the radical criticism formulated in the 1970s. In European cities affected by the explosion of a new urban tourism (Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Venice), anti-tourism movements have emerged, gaining traction in the media and academia, sometimes forcing local authorities to question, in more or less concrete terms, their tourist attractiveness policies.In this context, the World Tourism Organisation (UNWTO) published two reports in 2018 examining the phenomenon of overtourism and proposing courses of action. What is the significance of this intervention by the organisation reputed to be the global regulator of tourism? This paper seeks to answer this question by situating this initiative in the long history of the UN agency’s publications, most of which are dedicated to framing international statistics, over a period spanning from the 1960s to the 2024 publication of a new doctrinal document dedicated to the development of international statistics on “sustainable tourism”.The framing of international statistics is one of the main intervention tools of UN agencies. This paper provides an opportunity to revisit how this works, placing the controversy surrounding overtourism at the heart of the analysis. This perspective reveals the variations in the orientation of the policies that support them, and more recently the emergence of environmental concerns at all levels of international agencies. In a transversal manner, this chosen lens of statistical governance reminds us how this quantification of the world depends, almost fundamentally, on political arbitrations concerning the choices of what should be counted and how.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Tourism by the numbers: data, politics, and overtourism in Venice
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In recent debates on overtourism, tourism statistics have played a significant role. This analysis examines how tourism mobility is measured and how numerical data are mobilised for political purposes by various stakeholders, ranging from activists to city administrators. This article aims to reveal that tourism statistics, the technologies employed in their production, and the discourses surrounding them are shaped by distinct political perspectives and it seeks to uncover the reasons and mechanisms behind the quantification of tourism and overtourism in an urban context where tourist activity appears to have reached a critical threshold.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Pour un usage raisonné des données de téléphonie mobile dans l’analyse de la fréquentation d’une station balnéaire. Le cas de Cabourg (France)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Connected devices became widespread at the turn of the 2000s and 2010s. Their use in travel, especially for tourism or leisure, generates digital traces that constitute a massive data source for observing mobility. Among them, mobile phone data can potentially enrich the observation and analysis of mobilities. Therefore, many territories and tourism stakeholders are seizing this massive data as part of their visitors monitoring and observation policies. However, while coastal areas are major tourist destinations, there is very little work devoted to a critical approach to these data in seaside towns. Through a study carried out in Cabourg, a resort on the Normandy coast, we examine the benefits and limitations of using mobile phone data and advocate for a reasoned and contextualised use at a time when the impact of tourism is the subject of much debate.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Prendre la mesure de la diversité des personnes de passage dans les destinations touristiques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the “other visitors” in tourist destinations, often rendered invisible by traditional statistical categories that primarily distinguish between residents, tourists, and migrants. I examine in this article how official definitions of tourism, inherited from the 1929 crisis, mask a considerable diversity of travellers: seasonal workers, students, caregivers, patients, refugees, artists, etc. The study draws on three approaches: UNWTO statistics, mobile phone data (Orange’s Flux Vision Tourism), and the Venetian experiment with an entry tax. These analyses reveal the diversity of “other” people and show that they represent up to half of all presences in some destinations. The article highlights their potential for the ecological transition of tourism: longer stays, less distant geographical origins, lower-carbon local mobility. It advocates for better recognition of this diversity in territorial policies and a more inclusive approach to hospitality.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A measured debate: the quantification of (over)tourism in Lucerne, Switzerland
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Lucerne is a major destination for tourists and day-trippers in Switzerland. The production of statistics and data on tourism involves several actors and a variety of sources in Lucerne, which we refer to as a tourism quantification system. Adopting a critical approach of quantification, this paper analyses the structuring and current developments of the tourism quantification system in Lucerne, focusing specifically on the issue of ‘overtourism’. Indeed, the debate on certain excesses of tourism in Lucerne mobilises quantitative information on tourism in discourses, and leads to new forms of measurement of the tourism phenomenon, as well as to measures of regulation for certain aspects of tourism. However, these new forms of measurement do not yet provide regular data sources, and do not appear to be in a position to replace traditional sources of statistics in the foreseeable future.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Examining challenges and opportunities related to unconventional data sources for sustainable tourism
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The integration of unconventional data sources, such as mobile positioning and user-generated content, into tourism research has been widely discussed, yet their broader implications for sustainable tourism remain underexplored. This study aims to address this research gap by critically examining the challenges and opportunities associated with these data sources in enhancing sustainable tourism management. Utilising document analysis and semi-structured interviews with corporate representatives in Switzerland, this research identifies nine key data sources grouped into mobility, utility consumption, and financial/business data categories. The findings reveal the potential of these data sources to provide granular insights into tourism patterns, while highlighting challenges related to data sharing, quality, and privacy. Theoretical implications suggest a paradigm shift in stakeholder relationships and the validity of unconventional data for capturing tourist behaviour. Managerial implications emphasise the need for collaborative projects, predictive analysis, and data sharing for improved tourism governance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Quantifier la fréquentation dans les espaces naturels protégés : comparaison et limites de trois dispositifs de mesure
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The conservation of protected natural areas is attracting growing interest from visitors, prompting environmental professionals to intensify their efforts to reduce the pressures faced by these fragile ecosystems. This is a challenging task in a context where such spaces are increasingly sought after by both local residents and tourists. While visitor reception to protected areas is an essential component of their management, it is crucial to ensure that this access takes place under the best possible conditions, both for the natural environments themselves and for the nature experience they offer to visitors. This article highlights the results of a data collection campaign conducted on properties managed by the Conservatoire du littoral in mainland France, using new technologies to better understand visitor use and the ways in which tourist flows intersect and shape these spaces. The technologies employed are diverse – including pedestrian counters, mobile phone network detection, and questionnaires – and ultimately produce mixed results. While they reveal valuable insights into visitation dynamics, their deployment raises numerous practical challenges, and the limited precision of some of the data collected reduces their usefulness for the managers of these protected natural areas.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: An introduction to ‘skammvinnur tourism’: when humans interact with an unexpected walrus in Suðureyri (Iceland)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The unexpected appearance of a walrus (Odobenus rosmarus) in Suðureyri, Iceland, in November 2023 provided a rare opportunity to investigate ‘skammvinnur tourism’ – a concept we define as short-term wildlife encounters involving vagrant or migratory species. Unlike traditional wildlife tourism, these fleeting encounters are unplanned and occur in unpredictable locations, presenting unique challenges for both researchers and visitors. This study documented visitor interactions with the walrus over a 3-hour and 45-minute observation period, revealing that the rarity of the event influenced visitor behaviour, with individuals displaying heightened curiosity and a recognition of the encounter’s uniqueness. Using a multivariate analysis method (the Factor Analysis of Mixed Data or FAMD), environmental factors, particularly light, were found to significantly impact the behaviour of both the walrus and visitors. Additionally, the unanticipated nature of skammvinnur tourism presents significant challenges for researchers, as fieldwork cannot be planned or prepared in advance. This article proposes skammvinnur tourism as a distinct form of wildlife tourism, requiring its own framework for study, given the unpredictable and unique human-animal interactions it generates.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La naissance des Myrmidons chez Ovide
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The episode of the birth of the Myrmidons (Metamorphoses, Book VII) demonstrates Ovid’s delight in storytelling and his virtuosity in layering Virgilian quotations. The story is above all a sombre response to the bugonia, the marvellous rebirth of the bees that closes the Georgics. The metamorphosis of the ants is not a founding myth, as it is only a one-off episode intended to provide a battalion for an Athenian war against Minos. The population of Aegina is reborn, but only to follow Cephalus on his military expedition, and it is not certain that many of the young people will return to their homeland. The miracle therefore leads to nothing but a new war. The reader is thus confronted with a dizzying question about the hope for a renewal of Rome.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Considérations sur l’image du singe dans le monde antique. Le mythe des Cercopes entre iconographie et sources littéraires
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The paper is an interpretive survey of the legend of the Cercopes, a myth widespread in archaic and classical times that revolves on a peculiar kind of divine punishment: the metamorphosis of human beings into apes. The juxtaposition of literary sources and iconographic sources makes it possible to identify two main narrative strands: one, serious, is in fact part of the larger cycle of the labours of Heracles; the other, comic, may be regarded as a variant of the mythical theme featuring the hero himself and other satirical figures. In the comic variant a crucial role is played by the name Κέρκωψ, to be interpreted as “with the face in front of the tail”, that is to say, in front of Heracles’ posterior or genitals; another meaning of the name Κέρκωψ, related to the Cercopes’ impudence, can be traced back to a sexual metaphor still widespread to this day. A connection can also be established between the comic variant and well-known scenes, common both in archaic and classical times, of attempted theft of Heracles’ weapons by satyrs and sileni. These scenes may be taken as narrative devices meant to support the metamorphosis into apes well attested for the Italiotic area; in particular, the ape’s traits are counterbalanced by the Heraclean attribute of μελάμπυγος.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Euripide zoologue : Les Bacchantes entre l’anatomie et la politique
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In the Bacchae, Euripides reflects a concern with the anatomical description of bodies, in keeping with the advances and innovations of contemporary medicine, physiology, and zoology. Passages from the tragedy are compared to a Hippocratic text, On the Articulations, and to the apocryphal correspondence between Democritus and Hippocrates. The zoological and anatomical perspective in the Bacchae becomes a powerful tool for exploring the colossal crisis of contemporary Athens. The fragmentation and dissolution of human and animal nature thus take on a political dimension.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Poésie de la médecine vétérinaire. À propos de culpam ferro compesce chez Virgile, Georg. III, 468
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The verse from Georgics III, 468, ‘punish the fault with iron’, can be interpreted in various ways: it refers either to the surgical treatment of a sheep disease, which remains to be determined, or to the preventive slaughter of the first animal affected by a contagious disease. An examination of the use of this expression in later literature shows that Latin authors considered both meanings, depending on the literary genre in which they were writing. We must therefore consider the technical aspect of the treatment, comparing Virgil’s text with that of Columella on the same subject. This allows us to understand that it is not necessarily scabies, but another contagious disease of sheep such as sheep pox or foot rot, and that it is unlikely that Virgil envisaged slaughtering the first sick sheep. From this perspective, culpa should not be taken as a synonym for “disease”, but as a reproach for the “fault” of the shepherd, whose negligence led to the disease.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La nivrée chez Oppien de Cilicie (IV, 647-693)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The poem written by Oppian concerning fishing has a passage about fish poisoning at the end of book IV (647-693). After a first explanation of this passage, we show (particularly through a comparison with modern witnesses) that it probably contains a certain amount of first hand scientific information. We also intend to show that the pharmakon used for this operation is certainly typical of general Greek speculations concerning the pharmakon, but that it also reveals the way Oppian thinks, in the whole poem, about the links between marine and terrestrial life-forms, and about the cunning their relations entail. The pharmakon, in fact, seems to be a matter imbued with the actors’ intentions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La fourmi dans les Géorgiques de Virgile : un minuscule à décrypter
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The ant appears frequently in ancient literature before Virgil mentions it twice in Book I of the Georgics. Its presence, at once minute and yet highly meaningful, invites a closer examination. This paper aims to demonstrate how and why the ant is embedded within the scientific discourse of the Virgilian work through the medium of poetry. Both the farmer and the reader are encouraged to decipher the ant’s actions and sentiments in order to engage in a reflection on all living beings. Particular attention will be given to the complex issue of labor, on different scales (that of the ant in relation to the farmer, and that of human labour in relation to nature).

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Des insectes et des hommes dans l’épopée grecque archaïque
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The purpose of this paper is to outline the contours of insect poetics in ancient Greek epic poetry, beyond the singular poetics specific to each insect species or each work in the corpus. First I examine the different modes of interaction between insects and humans in the texts : from contiguity to analogy, insects are both with and like humans. The insect is then analyzed as an instrument of a significant change of scale, panoramic or close-up. Once the disproportion between man and insect is thus abolished, the insect often represents the gulf that separates the human condition from the divine condition. However, it does not express the insignificance of humans, as it ultimately proves to be the vehicle for a poetics of attentive observation and care.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le Taureau dans l’Urania de Giovanni Pontano (1429-1503) : un animal aux confins du Ciel et de la Terre
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The bull is one of the most common animals in ancient societies. It also appears in ancient astrology, invested with a symbolic value of natural power, linked to the spring renewal of the year. Giovanni Pontano, a 15th-century Italian humanist with a keen interest in astronomy, devotes a long passage to it in his Latin poem Urania sive de stellis. Responding to questions posed by ancient authors about the origin of the catasterism of an animal predisposed to become the protector of agricultural work, the humanist elaborates a mythological fable, in the manner of Ovid, to explain the domestication of the animal. The aim of this study is to explore the originality of this mythopoietic invention and its implications.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les animaux parlants dans les Phénomènes d’Aratos
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In their attempts to interpret and anticipate the meteorological phenomena that punctuate their lives, human beings try to find signs in nature that could guide them in their efforts. Among these signs, they observe in particular the behavior of animals. In his Phenomena, Aratus devotes considerable space to the predictions that can be drawn from these observations: animals send evocative signs to humans, and the poet seizes on this non-verbal message to construct his own poetic and scientific discourse on meteorology. I attempt to show how Aratus’ writing combines scientific considerations and strictly poetic work regarding these animal evocations, which are presented in the form of “poetic” lists. Aratus plays on the sound material of names and verse, but also on the signifying effects of accumulation and organization of the series. It is through this poetic work that Aratus manages to give not only body, but also voice to these mute animals.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Enjeux sociolinguistiques et typographiques de la traduction du « Petit prince » en langue algérienne (variété de Mazouna)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: By departing from the norms of Standard Arabic, the translation of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry’s emblematic work Petit Prince into Algerian dialect raises sociolinguistic, and typographic questions. Written in October 2023 by Mohammed Amin Benaribi and Khayreddine Arrouche, this adaptation—titled الصغير الأمير (Al-Amir Al Saghir) and rendered in the regional variety known as “Mazouni”—employs linguistic strategies specific to this dialect. Through a contrastive analysis of the source text and its transposition into Algerian Arabic, this study examines the status and legitimation of Darija within the Algerian literary field. It also sheds light on the sociolinguistic stakes of this translation dynamic, particularly regarding the valorization of so-called "minor" languages. In both form and content, the manuscript reflects a desire among the younger generation of Algerian writers to transcend cultural boundaries and to revitalize the Algerian language through the plurilingual potential of “Petit Prince”.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Lire Fahla de Rabah Sebaa : entre arabe algérien, graphie latine et horizon d’attente du lecteur algérien
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article offers an analysis of Rabeh Sebaa’s novel Fahla by combining three theoretical frameworks: sociolinguistics, Hans Robert Jauss’s reception theory, and Umberto Eco’s interpretive semiotics. The central hypothesis is that the use of Algerian Arabic transcribed in the Latin alphabet constitutes an aesthetic and ideological strategy that reshapes the reception of the text by challenging traditional literary norms. This linguistic choice subverts the scriptural hierarchies based on Standard Arabic and French, creating an unprecedented space of legitimacy for a language long marginalized. The main objective is to examine how this hybrid writing transforms the horizon of expectations of contemporary Algerian readers and shapes a cooperative reader, capable of interpreting the linguistic, cultural, and identity cues embedded in the text. It also aims to identify the skills that Fahla presupposes in its readers to fully grasp the scope of its linguistic framework. The methodology combines a sociolinguistic textual analysis focusing on sequences in Algerian Arabic and instances of code-switching, along with a reception study conducted with twenty Master’s students in linguistics. Bilingual passages were examined to identify their narrative and discursive functions, then presented to readers to assess their expectations, reactions, and the surprise effects triggered by unconventional spellings. The analysis of gaps between expectations and actual reception shows that Fahla shifts the boundaries of the literary field, reveals vernacular language practices, and establishes a new way of reading contemporary Algerian novels. Thus, Sebaa’s scriptural act emerges as both a strategy of linguistic revalorization and a driver of aesthetic renewal in the literary sphere.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Problématique de la langue et enjeux de la transcription dans la littérature populaire algérienne
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Situated at the intersection of linguistic anthropology and cultural semiotics, this study interrogates the discursive and ideological stakes of transcribing Algerian popular literature. It examines the epistemological rupture induced by the shift from orality—defined by embodied performance, co-presence, and contextual dynamism—to the written form, which imposes closure, permanence, and textual abstraction. Rejecting the notion of language as a neutral medium, the study posits it as a culturally inscribed, meaning-generating system. The analysis unfolds across four interrelated levels—phonetic, lexical, semantic, and narrative—revealing the layers of discursive displacement and semiotic loss that accompany inscription. To mitigate such disruptions, the research proposes two converging strategies: the use of digital technologies to preserve oral performance as a multimodal event, and interpretive translation that reframes popular utterances within their symbolic-cultural matrix. The study ultimately advocates for a model of textual mediation that safeguards the expressive integrity of oral traditions while harnessing the affordances of contemporary archiving and transmission technologies.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Écrire les langues nationales en Algérie : enjeux graphiques, pratiques sociales et idéologies linguistiques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article explores the complex relationship between language(s) of writing and writing system(s) of language in Algeria, a country shaped by deep linguistic diversity and a dense political history. Through a comparative theoretical analysis of tamazight and the Algerian Arabic dialect, the study highlights graphic issues as key indicators of glottopolitical, identity-based, and pedagogical tensions. The choice of script is not a mere normative exercise but a deeply symbolic act involving ideological, historical, and cultural dimensions. While tamazight navigates between Tifinagh, Latin, and Arabic scripts within a contested standardization process, the Algerian Arabic language is increasingly written in digital spaces, particularly through Latin-based transliterations, despite the absence of formal recognition. The article underlines the growing gap between top-down language planning and actual linguistic practices, shedding light on a bottom-up dynamic of vernacular innovation. Ultimately, it calls for a rethinking of graphic plurality not as a threat to national unity but as a vector for recognition, participation, and inclusion.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Faits et idéologies dans la question de la graphie pour la langue amazighe
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cultural policy issues in Algeria are at the heart of the question of the Amazigh alphabet. Writing and its written product spelled with the Latin script essentially reflect this state of affairs. This product needs perfecting, but remains undeniable. “A fait accompli” which may serve as a basis for an appropriate language policy decision. Used symbolically, and suspected of instrumentalization, the Tifinagh script struggles to keep up with the quality of the writings produced by the Latin script. To mitigate this suspicion, Tifinagh needs to be used as a tool for cultural creation and literary innovation, and as an editorial instrument for pedagogical practices as is the case with the Latin script. This also requires a total break with the “patrimonialist” vision towards the Amazigh language, and its promotion through a project aiming explicitly at its modernization sustained by an appropriate budget liable to gain the confidence of its defenders whose feeling of marginalization and exclusion remains strong despite some encouraging concessions in favour of “amazighness”. Presented as a requirement for the promotion of Tamazight, the Arabic script illustrates the relationship between Amazigh and supporters. For them, Arabic must dominate everywhere over Tamazight, while the defenders of Tamazight require on behalf of the socio-historical data which constitute “Algerianity”, the co-officiality of the two languages.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les idées linguistiques de Mouloud Mammeri (1917-1989) : retour sur l’œuvre berbérisante d’une figure emblématique du renouveau culturel berbère
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Adopting the perspective of historians of the language sciences – which entails a fairly broad definition of the concept of “linguistics” – this paper aims to revisit the work that the writer and anthropologist Mouloud Mammeri devoted to the study of Berber languages and the development of linguistic tools for these languages.The goal of this reflection is to identify the “linguistic ideas” (in the broad sense of knowledge about language and its study) held by this author regarding Berber languages. After a brief critical reading of his work – focused on his literary and linguistic writings – the paper examines his contributions particularly in the fields of grammar, neology/terminology, and the standardization of writing based on the Latin alphabet. In conclusion, it puts forward for discussion a hypothesis about Mouloud Mammeri’s projected vision concerning the linguistic planning of the Berber language.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’enseignement du/en berbère en Algérie et la question de la graphie
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study explores Algerian parents’ representations of the Berber language and their attitudes towards its teaching and writing system. Despite the official recognition of Tamazight in 2016, its integration into the educational system remains a sensitive and controversial issue, mainly due to regional and identity-based divisions. The research seeks to address several questions : What does Berber language represent for Algerian parents ? Are they in favor of its teaching ? Do they accept its use for teaching scientific subjects ? Which writing system do they prefer ? To answer these questions, a questionnaire survey was conducted among 200 parents (100 in Béjaïa and 100 in Oran), two regions differing both linguistically and geographically. The results reveal a strong symbolic legitimacy of Berber but an uneven educational acceptance : respondents from Béjaïa are largely supportive of its teaching, unlike those from Oran. Teaching scientific subjects in Berber is rejected in both regions. As for the writing system, the divide is clear : the Latin script dominates in Béjaïa, while the Arabic script is preferred in Oran. These findings highlight the need for a clear language policy decision regarding the writing system in order to further enhance social and educational interest in Berber.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’écriture littéraire plurilingue et la construction identitaire à l’ère du numérique : étude du cas de Sarah Rivens sur Wattpad
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study examines identity construction and plurilingual writing practices in digital literature through the case of Captive by Sarah Rivens, published on Wattpad. Drawing on a sociolinguistic perspective and digital discourse analysis, the research approaches the text not as a closed literary object but as a techno-discursive environment shaped by languages, writing practices, and community interactions. The analysis—supported by a technical sheet of the novel, selected excerpts, and reader comments—reveals a hybrid writing style combining French, English, and Algerian Arabic. Each language fulfills a specific narrative and symbolic function, contributing to a plural voice that reflects an identity in constant negotiation within a linguistic and cultural “in-between” space. Findings also show that the digital environment reconfigures authorial posture: the writer is no longer the sole source of meaning but becomes a node within a network of interactions. Through comments and reinterpretations, readers actively participate in meaning-making, redistributing enunciative authority and contributing to a collective construction of the narrative. This participatory ecosystem transforms the literary work into a dynamic process where emotions, values, and cultural belongings are continuously renegotiated. Overall, the study highlights the emergence of a connected literary aesthetics among young Algerian writers—an aesthetics marked by linguistic plurality, participation, and transnational openness, reflecting broader transformations of contemporary literary practices in the digital age.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La paratopie linguistique foncière de l’expression littéraire algérienne comme résultante d’une situation sociolinguistique
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Recent works in sociolinguistics such as those of Ibtissem Chachou, Abderrezak Dourari or Abdou Elimam highlight a multilingual reality intrinsic to Algeria, both diachronic and synchronic. This multilingualism manifests itself through various processes, from Apuleius of Madaura and Saint Augustine to the most recent authors. Algerian literature in its pratical reality, whether expressed in French, Arabic, the so-called Tamazigh languages, or even in Darijah or English, actually challenges this chimerical monolingualism that some call for. This paper uses discourse analysis to demonstrate the fundamental paratopia of Algerian literary discourse that results from the multiplicity of co-present languages. A multilingualism that will manifest itself in the texts of of extreme contemporary authors through alloglotism: a writing with a primary language that incorporates fragments in the different languages ​​co-existing in the Algerian linguistic landscape. A trend that appears to have been initiated by of Rachid Boudjedra or Tahar Ouattar and later identified in those of Mustapha Benfodil, Inâam Bayoudh, Nihed El-Alia and Lynda Chouiten.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Écriture de l’entrelangue : stratégies hétérolinguistiques et hétéroglossiques dans Kiffe kiffe demain et Kiffe kiffe hier ? De Faïza Guène

The study primarily relies on a poetic reading aimed at unveiling the heterolinguistic and heteroglossic strategies employed by the author, which contribute to the uniqueness of her narrative voice. Simultaneously, a sociocritical approach is adopted to shed light on the popular dimension that permeates her writing style—both in the choice of linguistic registers and in the representation of social realities from urban peripheries. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Appropriation du français et hybridité linguistique dans Terre des femmes de Nassira Belloula
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In Algeria, the use of one or several languages in a literary text is never innocent, as it is rooted in a deliberate scriptural choice that embodies linguistic hybridity, one shaped by multiple identity and cultural factors. Terre des femmes (2014), by Algerian writer Nassira Belloula, once again crystallizes this issue of coexistence and interaction among idioms within the materiality of writing. This article sheds light on this linguistic hybridity and on how French is instrumentalized as a scriptural language capable of accommodating the mixture of languages and dialects that emerges within it. In this novel of « difference », literary onomastics, through anthroponyms and toponyms, constitutes a privileged site for the insertion of linguistic and referential strangeness, perceptible from the very beginning of the text and extending to its very core. Furthermore, lexical borrowings appear as vectors of exchange and dialogue between the language of writing, French, and the linguistic and cultural referents specific to Algeria, a country of multilingualism.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Multilinguisme et déconstruction narrative : héritage et réinvention en littérature algérienne contemporaine
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Contemporary Algerian literature, like the Nouveau Roman, is characterized by a multiple commitment and a plurilingual writing that renews the way of telling History. The young writers of this new generation are illustrated by their use of French, classical and dialectal Arabic, as well as other languages, creating polyphonic works that reflect the identity and historical complexity of Algeria. Through their narrative experiments and their desire to question colonial legacies, these authors actively, participate in the reconstruction of a collective memory and the invention of a living and plural Algerian identity. Their political, social and cultural commitment goes beyond literature to reflect deeply on the contemporary issues of the country. The central question we ask is the following: how does the new generation of Algerian writers, by their repetitive use of official and national languages, redefine the writing of History and identity in their works? To address this issue, weadopt a cross-methodology combining stylistic and linguistic analysis of the texts, in order to study their polyphony and hybridity, as well as a thematic approach Focused on the political, identity and social commitment of the authors. This approach allows us to understand how these writers, through their plurilingual narrative experimentation, actively participate in the reconstruction of a plural collective memory and in the reinvention of an open Algerian identity, in a context marked by "ruins" histories of the colonial and postcolonial past.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Langue d’écriture et citoyenneté culturelle : entre choix individuel et mémoire collective en contexte algérien
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article addresses the question of language choice in Algerian literary/cultural production and links it to that of cultural citizenship in the postcolonial context due to linguistic plurality. The aim is to understand how the appropriation of French, Arabic or Tamazight takes place within a dialogue between collective memory, individual strategies and sociopolitical situation, while each of these languages has its history and power. The questioning revolves around two axes: does the scriptural choice engage an identity and citizen positioning? And how do these choices impact educational practices as well as the public space in Algeria? The analysis carried out is interdisciplinary: sociolinguistics, linguistic anthropology, and postcolonialism. With a solid theoretical framework, the study is divided into a practical part itself articulated in literary case studies (authors in French, Arabic and Tamazight), investigation of school uses and discursive analysis of varied corpora (literary, academic and media texts). The results indicate that the language of writing is not a simple preference but proceeds to the construction of an active and inclusive citizenship associating heritages, resistances and innovations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Poétiques du désaccord : subjectivités algériennes et langue française en crise dans deux romans contemporains
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article explores identity and intercultural issues in Algerian literature written in French through a comparative analysis of Houris by Kamel Daoud and Au vent mauvais by KaoutherAdimi. By articulating the concepts of writing language, postcolonial memory and literary subjectivation, it aims to understand how these two novels problematize national belonging and openness to otherness within their distinct aesthetics. The methodology combines thematic reading with narratological and sociocritical approaches. The analysis shows that while Houris proposes a provocative hybridization between tradition and modernity through a transgressive use of French, Au vent mauvais adopts a more introspective and minimalist form, expressing a cultural disinheritance. Through these narratives of dislocation, contemporary Algerian fiction redefines the contours of a postnational Francophonie, balancing local rootedness and global circulation. Underlying this process is a recomposition of the Algerian literary field, where the French language becomes a space of subjective reinvention and a vector of transcultural interaction.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Langue(s) d’écriture et écriture(s) de langue en Algérie : pluralité et projets de société à l’horizon 2025
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the linguistic and graphic diversity of contemporary Algerian literature, going beyond mere artistic choice. It analyzes how Algerian authors, through their preferences for French, Amazigh, or Algerian Arabic (Darija), and their choice of scripts (Latin, Arabic, Tifinagh), reflect and influence the country’s societal projects. The persistence of French is seen as a reappropriation and a window to universality, while the affirmation of vernacular languages is an activist act for identity recognition and democratization. The preference for Latin script, even for Algerian Arabic, signals a desire for modernity and accessibility, contrasting with the difficult adoption of Tifinagh despite its symbolic weight. Ultimately, this literary and linguistic diversity is perceived as a crucial asset for Algeria in 2025, challenging the country to build an inclusive national unity that values all its voices and multiple identities.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Langues profanes, message sacré : étude du rapport du plurilinguisme au féminisme dans la confrérie soufie alawiya
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines how the Alâwiyya Sufi order, through the work of Cheikh Khaled Bentounès (Sufism, the Heart of Islam), redefines the relationship between language, spirituality, and identity. Heir to a mystical tradition open to the world, the Alâwiyya path embraces linguistic plurality—Classical Arabic, vernacular Arabic, Kabyle, and French—as a space for reconciling the sacred and the profane. Drawing on a qualitative analysis of Sufi discourse and theoretical insights from sociolinguistics, gender studies, and the theory of symbolic power, the study highlights how the French language, long perceived as an instrument of domination, is reconfigured here as a vehicle for spiritual universality. From this perspective, Alâwiyya multilingualism is not merely a matter of expression but an inclusive and hermeneutic stance that rehabilitates women’s voices and the humanistic dimension of Sufism. The diversity of languages thus becomes the locus of a transcendence of linguistic, cultural, and gender hierarchies, fostering an experience of unity lived through difference.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le corps à corps de l’écrivain avec les langues dans la littérature francophone
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: French-speaking writer, caught up in the demands and geopolitical contexts is forced to think about his relationship with languages and otherness. It is clear that writing ultimately reveals the French-speaking writer’s struggle with the French language, a consequence of the discrepancies and difficulties inherent in the imposition of inadequate standards and references, which constitute obstacles and risks to their expression. We will examine how writers feel about the demands imposed by canons that do not take into account or are unable to translate their place in the world, their sensibilities and their deepest aspirations. After providing a brief historical overview and reviewing the various manifestations of questioning, domination and marginalisation suffered by Francophone writers, this article will focus on observing the modes of operation illustrating the reactions to the malaise existing in the literary Francophonie, as expressed by Ali Zamir in his novel, Anguille sous roche and Mohamed Mbougar Sarr in La plus secrète mémoire des hommes, both through writing techniques and the themes addressed.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les écrivains algériens et la langue française : une histoire d’amour ou un choix stratégique ?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article is essentially based on a historical and sociological approach to examine the relationship of French-speaking Algerian writers to the French language, both during the colonial period and during the postcolonial period. It examines the various motivations that lead them to write in a language associated with a painful colonial history experienced by the Algerian people, rather than in their mother tongues, Arabic or Berber. The study shows that this linguistic choice results, for writers of the colonial period, resulted from a constraint imposed by the colonial system itself, while for writers of the postcolonial period, it is often a conscious choice, driven by aesthetic or strategic considerations, notably the desire to free themselves from social limits and to inscribe their works within a perspective of universality.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Discursive Cultures and Genres in Japanese Textbooks of English and French as Foreign Languages
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Over the past few decades, contrastive discourse analysis (CODA) has enabled researchers to describe the characteristics of discourse communities across countries. However, its potential goes beyond national and linguistic frontiers. In this paper, I examine a corpus of English and French textbooks created in the same geographical area, i.e., Japan, for the same target audience. Below superficial homogeneity, the corpus conceals numerous differences. To tackle them, I adopt an approach centred on the “etic”/“emic” distinction that CODA draws from. The aim is twofold: to discover the discursive cultures underlying the textbooks, on the one hand, and to gather an internal (emic) description of the genre, on the other. Through an analysis of linguistic markers, text types, and intertextuality/interdiscourse, this study highlights the emergence of two discursive communities (Japanese and French), irrespective of the language in which they express themselves.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Chronotopic Dimensions of Authoritarianism and Violence in Brazilian and Austrian Autobiographical Testimonies
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Memories of historical traumas (war, natural disaster, genocide, dictatorship, etc.) continue to play an important role in discourse and, more broadly, in social relations in several countries. In the context of the problematic memory work carried out in Brazil regarding the civil–military dictatorship and in Austria regarding the Shoah and the Second World War, a resurgence of life writing embedded in literary discourse can be observed in both countries, and among authors originating from them. This contribution presents the results of a contrastive analysis of autobiographical testimonies of this kind. Within the methodological framework of contrastive discourse analysis (von Münchow 2021) and inspired by the thought of Mikhail Bakhtin – particularly through the concept of the chronotope (1978 [1937-38]) – the study seeks to describe discursive representations of authoritarianism, repression, and violence according to three chronotopic dimensions: (1) the external dimension related to the reported events; (2) the external dimension related to the narratives; and (3) the internal dimension. The corpus comprises the narratives Ainda estou aqui (2015) by Marcelo Rubens Paiva, Volto semana que vem (2014) by Maria Pilla, Weiter leben (1992) by Ruth Klüger, and Vienna (2005) by Eva Menasse. The analyses highlight how autobiographical discourse, within each discursive culture, enables the articulation of individual and collective memory, thereby configuring forms of critical resistance to negationism, authoritarianism, and violence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Représenter l’identité dans les manuels d’anglais américain et de français langue étrangère
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cet article étudie la représentation de l’identité dans des manuels d’anglais américain et de français langue étrangère publiés au cours des cinq dernières années. Ancrée dans l’analyse du discours contrastive (ADC) et dans la théorie des métafonctions de Halliday, cette étude montre que les manuels de français considèrent l’apprenant comme un jeune dont l’identité correspond à celle de sa génération. Les manuels d’anglais américain, en revanche, considèrent l’apprenant comme un individu doté d’expérience et d’une identité émergente en tant que locuteur d’anglais. Un point commun aux manuels des deux langues est l’absence relative de représentations de l’orientation sexuelle. L’intégration de textes authentiques constitue un moyen de rendre visibles des identités diverses, mais, en tant qu’objets culturels, les manuels sont influencés par les objectifs commerciaux des auteurs. Ces résultats indiquent que l’étude des cultures discursives au sein de certains genres nécessite la prise en compte des intérêts commerciaux qui influencent leur production.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Representing Identity in American English and French Foreign Language Coursebooks
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the representation of learner identities through discourse in a selection of American English and French as a Foreign Language coursebooks published within the past five years. Anchored in contrastive discourse analysis and Halliday’s metafunctional theory, the analysis shows that French coursebooks view the learner as a young person whose identity aligns with that of his/her generation. In contrast, American English coursebooks see the learner as an individual with prior experiences and an emerging identity as an English speaker. A similarity among the coursebooks is the relative absence of representations of identity dimensions, such as sexual orientation. While authentic texts offer opportunities to provide visibility of diverse sexual identities, as cultural artefacts, coursebooks are influenced by their authors' commercial goals. These results indicate that investigating discursive cultures within specific discursive genres requires consideration of the commercial interests that shape their production.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Quelles cultures discursives et quels genres derrière les manuels d’anglais et de français au Japon ?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Au fil des années, l’analyse du discours contrastive (ADC) a permis d’éclairer des caractéristiques distinguant des communautés discursives situées dans des pays différents, mais son potentiel dépasse les frontières étatiques et linguistiques. Dans cette contribution, j’examine des ouvrages conçus à l’intérieur d’un même espace géographique et pour un même public, à savoir des manuels d’anglais et de français au Japon. Ce corpus apparemment homogène recèle en réalité de nombreuses oppositions. Ainsi, je propose une démarche fondée sur l’opposition entre « éticité » et « émicité » que mobilise l’ADC avec un double objectif : d’une part, faire émerger des traits des communautés discursives effectivement à l’œuvre dans les deux sous-ensembles du corpus (étique) et, de l’autre, obtenir une description interne (émique) du genre discursif du manuel scolaire de langues étrangère. Une analyse des marques linguistiques, des séquentialités textuelles et des traces d’intertextualité ou d’interdiscours permet de mettre en évidence l’émergence de deux communautés discursives, essentiellement japonaises et françaises, qui s’expriment à travers les langues.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’Analyse du discours contrastive. Comparer les cultures discursives à travers l’espace et le temps
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Dans cet article, l’auteure s’efforce de retracer son parcours de recherche d’une analyse du discours contrastive (ADC) « horizontale » (synchronique) vers une ADC « verticale » (diachronique) à travers la mise au jour empirique, la théorisation et l’instrumentalisation méthodologique de l’hétérogénéité des cultures discursives ainsi que des non-dits. Elle montre en quoi l’hétérogénéité des cultures discursives, loin de mettre en cause leur existence, souligne en réalité leur force. Elles sont à la fois dynamiques et stables, évoluant sans cesse sans pour autant perdre (toutes) les traces d’états antérieurs, ce qui, à la fois, rend une ADC horizontale pleinement opératoire – car cette approche permet de faire ressortir tout un réseau de représentations de statuts différents et datant de différentes époques, souvent contradictoires les unes par rapport aux autres – et confère un intérêt particulier à l’ADC verticale dans le but de retracer, voire de dater ces différentes couches de représentations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Contrastive Discourse Analysis: Comparing Discursive Cultures Across Space and Time
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In this article, the author traces her research journey from a “horizontal” (synchronic) approach to Contrastive Discourse Analysis (CODA) toward a “vertical” (diachronic) approach by empirically uncovering, theorizing, and methodologically operationalizing the heterogeneity of discursive cultures, as well as what remains unsaid. She demonstrates that the heterogeneity of discursive cultures, far from undermining their existence, highlights their strength. These discursive cultures are both dynamic and stable, constantly evolving while still retaining (some) traces of earlier states. This not only makes a horizontal CODA fully effective – by bringing to light a network of representations with different statuses and from different periods, often in contradiction with one another – but also lends particular value to vertical CODA, which aims to trace and even date these different layers of representations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les dimensions chronotopiques de l’autoritarisme et de la violence dans les témoignages autobiographiques brésiliens et autrichiens
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Les mémoires de traumatismes historiques (guerre, catastrophe naturelle, génocide, dictature, etc.) continuent de jouer un rôle majeur dans le discours et, plus largement, dans les relations sociales de nombreux pays. Dans le contexte d’un travail de mémoire problématique au Brésil concernant la dictature civile-militaire, et en Autriche à propos de la Shoah et de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, on observe, dans ces deux pays – ou chez des auteur·e·s issu·e·s de ces contextes – une recrudescence des écritures de vie inscrites dans le discours littéraire. Cette contribution présente les résultats d’une analyse contrastive de témoignages autobiographiques relevant de ce corpus. S’inscrivant dans le cadre méthodologique de l’Analyse du Discours Contrastive (von Münchow, 2021) et s’inspirant de la pensée de Mikhaïl Bakhtine – notamment du concept de chronotope (Bakhtine, 1978 [1937–1938]) –, l’étude vise à décrire les représentations discursives de l’autoritarisme, de la répression et de la violence selon trois dimensions chronotopiques : 1) la dimension externe liée aux faits rapportés ; 2) la dimension externe liée à l’énonciation du récit ; 3) la dimension interne. Le corpus comprend les récits Ainda estou aqui (2015) de Marcelo Rubens Paiva, Volto semana que vem (2014) de Maria Pilla, Weiter leben (1992) de Ruth Klüger et Vienna (2005) d’Eva Menasse. Les analyses mettent en évidence la manière dont le discours autobiographique permet d’articuler, dans chaque culture discursive, mémoire individuelle et mémoire collective, configurant ainsi des formes de résistance critique à l’oubli, à l’autoritarisme et à la violence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Parler des crises dans la presse écrite en France, en Estonie et aux États-Unis. Des corpus sur la pandémie de Covid-19 aux grands corpus diachroniques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cet article propose un ensemble d’analyses contrastives des discours médiatiques portant sur la notion et le lexème « crise » dans la presse écrite française, estonienne et américaine. Cette étude, qui s’inscrit dans un projet plus large sur les représentations discursives de la crise, mobilise plusieurs outils numériques (Hyperbase, Sketch Engine, Lexicoscope) et croise des corpus variés centrés sur la pandémie de Covid-19, puis élargis à une perspective diachronique. Trois axes sont développés : l’analyse des cooccurrences lexicales de termes liés à la notion de crise sur le plan thématique (« chercheur », « télétravail »), pour décrire les figures du savoir et du devoir ; l’étude des structures syntaxiques contenant des verbes modaux, afin d’identifier les actants saillants et leurs modalités d’action ; et enfin, l’examen de l’environnement lexical du mot « crise », pour évaluer l’évolution sémantique de ses usages dans des contextes de post-crise (2010 et 2024).

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le langage au service de la dépathologisation en France et aux États‑Unis : analyse contrastive de métadiscours antivalidistes numériques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cet article restitue les résultats d’une analyse contrastive de métadiscours produits par des cybermilitants antivalidistes français et étatsuniens. En nous appuyant sur un corpus d’environ 200 documents issus de réseaux socionumériques, blogs et forums, nous mettons au jour les représentations que ces militants se font du pouvoir pathologisant des mots. Nous examinons les procédés discursifs qu’ils déploient pour rendre certaines paroles illégitimes et disqualifier les usages d’une terminologie estimée oppressive, et distinguons métadiscours préventifs et correctifs. Si l’ensemble du corpus témoigne d’une conscience partagée de la performativité du langage et d’une volonté de valoriser la parole des personnes directement concernées, l’analyse montre que les recommandations terminologiques sont mieux intégrées aux États‑Unis, où les productions comportent des références implicites et des stratégies d’atténuation visant à préserver la face des « fautifs ». En France, on adopte un ton plus explicite et argumentatif, parfois radical, afin d’anticiper et contrer d’éventuelles contestations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Talking about Crises in the Written Press in France, Estonia and the United States. From Covid-19 Corpora to Large Diachronic Corpora
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article offers a set of contrastive analyses of media discourses involving the notion and lexeme “ crisis” in French, Estonian, and American print journalism. This study, which is part of a broader project on the discursive representations of crises, mobilizes several digital tools (Hyperbase, Sketch Engine, Lexicoscope) and crosses various corpora centered on the Covid-19 pandemic, then expanded to a diachronic perspective. Three main lines of inquiry are developed: the analysis of lexical co-occurrences of terms linked to the notion of crisis on a thematic level (“researcher”, “remote work”) to describe the figures of knowledge and obligation; the study of syntactic structures containing modal verbs, in order to identify the salient actants and their modalities of action; and finally, the examination of the lexical environment of the word “crisis” (crise), to evaluate the semantic evolution of its uses in post-crisis contexts (2010 and 2024).

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Depathologizing Language: A Contrastive Discourse Analysis of Online Anti‑Ableism Metadiscourse in France and the United States
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article presents the results of a contrastive discourse analysis of online anti-ableist metadiscourse in French and American contexts. Drawing on a corpus of approximately 200 posts from social media, blogs, and forums, it examines activists’ representations of the pathologizing nature of language and the discursive strategies they use to delegitimize oppressive terminology, employing both preventive and corrective metadiscourse. The findings indicate a shared awareness of language’s performative nature and a strong emphasis on centring the voices of those directly concerned. Contrasts emerge nonetheless: in the United States, terminological recommendations are more widely adopted, with typically toned-down corrections which save the face of those considered at “fault.” In France, metadiscourse tends to be more explicit, argumentative, and occasionally blunt, reflecting a desire to forestall resistance to linguistic prescriptions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Seventy Years of Occupation in French and Polish History Textbooks
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study examines discourses on the occupation during the Second World War in French and Polish history textbooks. Our objective is to examine how this dark period is named from the perspective of social representations and their modifications from the 1950s to the present. Thus, we will focus on the nouns (occupation and okupacja) and their specifying adjectives (“Hitler”/hitlerowski, “Nazi”/nazistowski, “Allemand” (German)/niemiecki and also Sovietique/sowiecki or radziecki and Italien/włoski) as well as figurative expressions (such as les années noires [“the dark years”]/ /w cieniu swastyki).). The study of naming practices reveals different discursive cultures and thus, the varied and dynamic social representations that were forged in France and Poland. They do not result from differences in referential universes but from two different ways of “narrating” reality.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le compliment dans les talk-shows en France et en Iran
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cet article traite du fonctionnement du compliment dans les talk-shows français et iraniens, à partir d’un corpus audiovisuel contrastif. À la faveur d’un double tertium comparationis, le genre talk-show d’une part, et l’acte de langage « complimenter » de l’autre, des points de rencontre ont pu être dégagés entre les corpus en amont des analyses. L’examen des données a toutefois mis en évidence, quelques différences. En français, le compliment, peu ritualisé, apparaît comme un marqueur d’appréciation ponctuel, souvent lié à la promotion d’œuvres culturelles. En persan, il s’inscrit dans le cadre du ta’ârof, rituel de politesse fortement codifié, et intervient fréquemment en ouverture pour valoriser l’invité(e) et instaurer un climat relationnel empreint de respect. L’étude met également en lumière la dimension multimodale de ces énoncés (verbale, para-verbale, non-verbale) et leurs effets interactionnels dans la gestion des faces, spécialement en persan.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Compliments in Talk Shows in France and Iran
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article explores how compliments are used in French and Iranian talk shows, based on a contrastive audiovisual corpus. Drawing on a dual tertium comparationis, the talk show genre on the one hand, and the speech act of complimenting on the other, points of convergence were identified between the corpora before the analyses. However, the examination of the data revealed some differences. In French, compliments, which are only weakly ritualized, tend to function as occasional markers of appreciation, often linked to the promotion of cultural works. In Persian, by contrast, compliments are embedded within the framework of ta’ârof, a highly codified politeness ritual, and are frequently offered at the opening of interactions to honor the guest and establish a respectful relational climate. The study also highlights the multimodal dimension of these utterances (verbal, paraverbal, and nonverbal) and their interactional effects on face management, particularly in Persian.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Soixante-dix ans d’occupation dans les manuels d’histoire français et polonais
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cette étude a pour objet les discours sur l’occupation pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale dans les manuels d’histoire français et polonais. Notre objectif est d’examiner les façons de nommer cette période sombre de l’histoire du point de vue des représentations sociales et de leurs modifications depuis les années 50 jusqu’à nos jours. Ainsi, nous nous intéressons aux noms « occupation » et okupacja, aux adjectifs qui les spécifient (« hitlérien »/ hitlerowski, « nazi »/ nazistowski, « allemand » /niemiecki, « soviétique » /sowiecki ou radziecki et « italien »/włoski, ainsi qu’aux expressions figurées (de type « les années noires » /w cieniu swastyki). L’étude de la nomination révèle différentes cultures discursives et par là, les représentations sociales variées et dynamiques qui se sont forgées en France et en Pologne. Elles ne résultent pas de différences d’univers référentiels, mais de deux manières différentes de « raconter » le réel.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Jugement professoral et influence du système de genre dans les bulletins scolaires
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The central objective of this research article is to explore how “reinforcing” or “subversive” discourse regarding gender stereotypes influences the evaluative judgment of PE teachers. Previous studies (Chalabaev, 2006 ; Moniotte and Poggi, 2014) reveal that students' gender impacts teachers’ expectations and judgments, even affecting report cards. Our article aims to deepen this question by examining teachers individually to determine if their discourse influences and is reflected in their professional judgment. Using the story-completion method, we will identify the “reinforcing” and “subversive” discourses present among teachers. Student report cards will then be analysed to see if student gender influences teachers' evaluations, revealing distinct expectations for girls and boys.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les perspectives professionnelles des enseignant·es-chercheur·es en début de carrière au prisme du genre
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The under-representation of women in the upper echelons of the higher education hierarchy appears in several international surveys. This article looks at the entry into the profession of teacher-researchers in French universities to determine whether this vertical inequality corresponds to individual decisions made over time or, on the contrary, taken in the first few years. The interviews we conducted revealed a whole range of obstacles that make it more difficult for women to achieve career advancement. The results of the questionnaire used in this study show differences in career prospects leading women, from the very first years, to invest more than men in teaching, to the detriment of research, and to postpone obtaining the habilitation to direct research, which is required to apply for the status of university professor.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Pour une approche praxéologique de l’intersectionnalité en éducation et formation(Volume 2)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Education, as a social and political field, is shaped by power relations that are constructed and articulated through multiple social systems of categorization: gender, race, class, disability, religion, and geographic origin. In the face of persistent inequalities and the plurality of educational experiences, intersectionality has emerged as an essential theoretical and methodological framework. Rooted in the foundational work of Black feminism, this paradigm makes it possible to move beyond isolated categorical analyses and understand the mechanisms of domination and marginalisation in their interdependence. This volume provides a critical overview of the uses of intersectionality in educational research and highlights studies that are actively exploring its practical application.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Retisser l'intersectionnalité dans l'histoire de l'éducation des filles au Congo colonial : le cas du Foyer Social d'Élisabethville (1934-1960)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In history of education, particularly with regard to colonial and women's education, the use of intersectionality as a method of analysing historical sources is growing rapidly. This study contributes to this body of research by (a) exploring how intersectionality can be operationalised in the history of education and by (b) illustrating its application in the specific case of girls' and women's education at the Elisabethville’s (Lubumbashi, DRC) Foyer Social during the Belgian Congo era (1934–1959). More specifically, following Danièle Kergoat's work, it seeks to demonstrate the consubstantiality and coextensiveness of relations of gender, race, class and age domination, to be retraced through the colonial archives of this educational institution for Congolese women and girls.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Analyser l’intersectionnalité par la méthode quantitative : profils de jeunes face à la cyberhaine
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article offers a critical reflection on the methodological implications of applying quantitative methods within intersectional research. It draws on the findings of a doctoral research examining the experiences of adolescent girls exposed to and/or victimized by cyberhate, in comparison with those of boys living in France. By adopting an intercategorical approach, the study explores heterogeneous profiles while considering a broad range of sociodemographic variables, including sex, age, parents’ socio-occupational category, ancestry, and vulnerability status. The findings indicate that belonging simultaneously to multiple minority groups is associated with a significantly higher risk of exposure to and victimization by cyberhate. The article seeks to move beyond the tendency to confine intersectional studies to qualitative approaches, highlighting the relevance and robustness of quantitative methods for advancing this field of research. It also provides recommendations to address the methodological challenges encountered in applying this approach.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Prendre en compte les rapports sociaux dans l’analyse de l’activité de travail des Accompagnant·es d’Elèves en Situation de Handicap
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article is the result of a research-intervention project in educational sciences aimed at analyzing the work activity of the support staff for students with disabilities (AESH, from the French acronym). The request made by the collective involved in this research guided the analysis toward social relations at work that produce a position of inferiority within the organization of schoolwork. As a result, the support staff experiences situations of exclusion within their workplace, whether in informal, semi-formal, or formal settings. However, their identity, particularly gender identity, also constitutes a resource for their work activity. The researcher therefore proposes a re-reading of the transcripts through the lens of gender, race, class, or disability to show that the decisions made by these workers are shaped by social relations. This article argues for the integration of an intersectional approach to complement the field of work analysis to better understand the social relations structuring the activity of education professionals.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La propriété immobilière face aux temporalités des marchés et de ses acteurs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While sociology has contributed to empirical studies on how interpersonal relationships shape economic action and how intermediaries guide consumer decisions, little attention has been paid to the temporalities of the capitalist regime and the temporal dispositions of actors empirically. During the 20th century, buying a house became one of the materialized milestones of the “American dream”, at the heart of the motivations and economic actions undertaken on real estate markets. Based on lines of inquiry from the sociology of market activity and economic sociology and an ethnographic survey conducted among real estate agents in a medium-sized city in the American Southwest, this article proposes to question the forms of temporalities at work in real estate ownership, work and transactions carried out by real estate agents. Combining theoretical considerations on the social and economic temporalities at work in real estate markets and field observations on how temporalities act, within a local real estate market, the article explores the conditions of emergence and the temporalities of the imposition of the ideology of real estate ownership, focuses on the temporalities of entrepreneurship among real estate agents, and analyses how tensions are exerted in the temporalities of transactions.
